docs.title: Case study: 150 signals on Vietnamese equities
docs.text:
We ran every daily signal in polars-anta (150 signals, 146 unique) through the library's own falsification pipeline on the most liquid stocks of the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE). The analysis plan was committed to Git before any results were computed, and the 2022-2026 holdout was evaluated only after the discovery results were committed.

Why Vietnam? HOSE is a retail-driven emerging market with daily price limits, no short selling for most investors and high trading costs. It is far less studied than US equities, which makes it a demanding out-of-sample test for signals that were designed elsewhere.

Question Result Signals tested 150 Effectively independent tests among them \(N_{\text{eff}} = 6.00\) Significant after multiple-testing correction (Romano-Wolf, 5% FWER) 71 Significant and stable over the discovery period (2014-2021) 64 Still significant in the locked holdout (2022-2026) 38 of 64 Significant long-only excess return after 60 bps round-trip costs 0

What this means

  • Most signals are variations of the same effect. 91 of 150 signals pass a naive \(p \le 0.05\) test, but their daily ICs move together so closely that they amount to only \(N_{\text{eff}} = 6.00\) independent tests. Much of this common component is short-term (5-day) reversal: removing it raises \(N_{\text{eff}}\) from 6.00 to 9.37.
  • The predictive power holds up out of sample. 38 of the 64 stable discovery signals remain significant in the holdout, with a median IC retention of 97.6%.
  • But it does not pay for itself. The strongest signals replace 63.8% to 87.2% of the portfolio every 5 days and break even at 20.5 bps round-trip at best, well below realistic costs. In addition, 65.5% of the top-10 signals' long-short spread in discovery (90.0% in holdout) comes from the short leg, which long-only investors cannot capture.

Read the full study in research/factor-zoo.md.

docs.title: What is polars-anta?
docs.text:
polars-anta (Alpha and Numerical Technical Analysis) is a quantitative finance library for market microstructure estimation, derivatives analytics, machine learning labeling and stationarity (AFML), cross-sectional factor engineering, statistical alpha evaluation, and execution-realistic vectorized backtesting in Python and Polars.

Built for quantitative researchers, proprietary trading desks, index futures strategists (e.g. VN30F1M, CME E-mini, Crypto Perpetuals), and systematic portfolio managers, polars-anta implements technical indicators, closed-form OLS regressions, 33 formulaic alphas from Kakushadze's 101 Formulaic Alphas, and portfolio evaluation tools directly as native Polars expressions (pl.Expr).

    B --> C["3. Factor Orthogonalization<br/>cs_winsorize, cs_zscore<br/>neutralize, orthogonalize (OLS)"]
    C --> D["4. Statistical Validation<br/>Newey-West HAC t-stat<br/>IC Decay Half-Life, PSR and DSR"]
    D --> E["5. Realistic Execution<br/>Next-Open/VWAP, Vol-Targeting<br/>No-Trade Buffer, MAE/MFE Ledger"]

docs.title: The 4 Research Pillars
docs.text: 1. Intraday Microstructure and Derivatives Aggregate tick/minute feeds into information-driven bars (resample_volume_bars, resample_dollar_bars, resample_imbalance_bars), stitch continuous futures contracts (stitch_futures_roll), track intraday session_vwap deviation z-scores, quantify order flow toxicity (vpin, ofi), and monitor carry and positioning (futures_basis, oi_regime). Resampling and Roll Guide | Microstructure Docs 2. Quant Machine Learning (AFML Primitives) Transform non-stationary price series into stationary, memory-preserving features via Fixed-Window Fractional Differentiation (frac_diff), generate path-dependent dynamic Triple-Barrier and Meta-Labeling targets (triple_barrier_labels), and extract multi-horizon OLS Trend-Scanning labels (trend_scanning_labels). Stats and FracDiff | AFML Labeling 3. Cross-Sectional Factor Validation Clip extreme outliers (cs_winsorize via Quantile/Z-Score/MAD), sector-neutralize (neutralize), strip multi-factor risk exposures via Modified Gram-Schmidt OLS projection (orthogonalize), and validate with Newey-West HAC t-statistics (ic_summary), Alpha Half-Life (ic_decay), and Deflated Sharpe Ratios (deflated_sharpe_ratio). Quant Theory Guide | Factor Eval 4. Execution-Realistic Vectorized Backtesting Simulate realistic fills at next-bar open, TWAP, or VWAP (execution_price="open"), enforce mandatory intraday EOD/roll session flatten masks (flat_mask), apply ex-ante volatility targeting (vol_target) and hysteresis turnover buffers (no_trade_buffer), and audit round-trip MAE/MFE trade ledgers (bt.trades()). Backtesting Engine | Multi-Asset Scaling

docs.title: Interactive Quantitative Workflows
docs.text:
Install polars-anta in seconds with zero C compiler requirements:

pip install polars-anta

Explore how polars-anta unifies derivatives microstructure, AFML feature engineering, cross-sectional factor orthogonalization, and realistic backtesting into fluent Polars pipelines:

1. Intraday Microstructure and Futures2. Quant ML (AFML Primitives)3. Cross-Sectional Factor Alpha4. Realistic Backtest and IC Validation 
import polars as pl
import polars_anta as pa  # Registers .anta and .ta namespaces

# 1. Stitch continuous futures contracts (backward, ratio or panama) and sample volume bars:
cont_df = raw_contracts.anta.stitch_futures_roll(method="backward")
vol_bars = cont_df.anta.resample_volume_bars(volume_threshold=5_000)

# 2. Extract session-anchored VWAP, order flow toxicity (VPIN, OFI), carry and open interest regimes:
deriv_features = vol_bars.with_columns(
    pl.col("close")
    .anta.session_vwap("high", "low", "volume", session_by="trading_date")
    .alias("svwap"),
    pl.col("close").anta.vpin("volume", period=20).alias("vpin_20"),
    pl.col("bid_price").anta.ofi("bid_size", "ask_price", "ask_size", period=5).alias("ofi_5"),
    pl.col("close").anta.futures_basis("spot_close", "days_to_expiry", period=20).alias("basis"),
    pl.col("close").anta.oi_regime("open_interest", period=1).alias("oi_state"),
).unnest("svwap", "basis", "oi_state")

# Memory-preserving stationary features (FFD) plus triple-barrier and trend-scanning labels:
ml_dataset = df.with_columns(
    pl.col("close").anta.frac_diff(d=0.4, window=20).over("symbol").alias("close_ffd"),
    pl.col("close")
    .anta.triple_barrier_labels(
        volatility=pl.col("close").pct_change().rolling_std(20),
        horizon=12,
        pt_mult=2.0,
        sl_mult=1.5,
        side=pl.col("primary_signal"),  # Enables binary meta_label {0.0, 1.0}
    )
    .over("symbol")
    .alias("tb"),
    pl.col("close")
    .anta.trend_scanning_labels(min_window=5, max_window=20)
    .over("symbol")
    .alias("ts"),
).unnest("tb", "ts")

alpha_df = panel_df.with_columns(
    (
        -pl.col("close").anta.ts_delta(5).over("symbol")
        * pl.col("volume").anta.ts_rank(20).over("symbol")
    ).alias("raw_alpha")
).with_columns(
    pl.col("raw_alpha")
    .anta.cs_winsorize(over="date", method="mad", threshold=3.0)
    .anta.cs_zscore(over="date", clip_bound=3.0)
    .anta.neutralize(by="sector", over="date", standardize=True)
    # Modified Gram-Schmidt OLS projection orthogonal to beta, size and volatility:
    .anta.orthogonalize(factors=["mkt_beta", "log_mcap", "vol_20"], over="date", standardize=True)
    .anta.ts_scale(a=1.0, over="date")
    .alias("pure_alpha_weight")
)

# 1. Autocorrelation-robust Newey-West HAC IC and multi-horizon alpha half-life:
eval_df = alpha_df.anta.forward_returns(periods=(1, 5, 10), group_by="symbol")
ic_stats = eval_df.anta.ic_summary("pure_alpha_weight", "fwd_ret_5", group_by="date", nw_lags=5)
decay_table = eval_df.anta.ic_decay(
    "pure_alpha_weight", horizons=(1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20), group_by="date"
)

# 2. Execution-realistic vectorized backtest with MAE and MFE excursion ledger:
bt = (
    df.anta.ema(12, alias="ema_12")
    .anta.ema(26, alias="ema_26")
    .anta.backtest(
        entries=pl.col("ema_12").anta.crosses_above("ema_26"),
        exits=pl.col("ema_12").anta.crosses_below("ema_26"),
        execution_price="open",  # Fill at next-bar open price
        flat_mask=pl.col("is_eod"),  # Force flat before ATC / overnight
        vol_target=0.15,  # 15% annualized volatility target
        no_trade_buffer=0.05,  # Suppress micro-rebalancing turnover
        fee_rate=0.0005,
        slippage_rate=0.0002,
    )
)
print(bt.report())
print(bt.trades())  # Round-trip trade ledger with PnL, holding_bars, MAE and MFE

docs.title: Core Mathematical and Systems Foundations
docs.text: Rather than iterating row-by-row in Python or opaque Cython loops, polars-anta reduces time-series regressions, fractional operators, and cross-sectional projections into closed-form algebraic identities compiled directly by Polars' Rust query engine:

docs.title: 1. Rolling OLS Slope via Exact WMA-SMA Algebraic Identity
docs.text:
By exploiting the exact linear identity between the Linearly Weighted Moving Average (\(\text{WMA}_n\)) and Simple Moving Average (\(\text{SMA}_n\)), rolling Ordinary Least Squares slope (\(\beta_{1,t}\)) and intercept (\(\beta_{0,t}\)) are evaluated in \(O(1)\) complexity per bar (112.4x faster than a pandas rolling().apply() baseline):

\[ \beta_{1,t} = \frac{6}{n - 1}\left(\text{WMA}_n(y)_t - \text{SMA}_n(y)_t\right), \qquad \beta_{0,t} = \text{SMA}_n(y)_t - \beta_{1,t}\frac{n - 1}{2} \]

docs.title: 2. Fixed-Window Fractional Differentiation (FFD)
docs.text:
Applies the binomial expansion of the backshift operator \((1 - B)^d\) over a fixed horizon \(W\) to achieve statistical stationarity while preserving long-memory cointegration at fractional order \(d \in (0, 1)\):

\[ \tilde{X}_t^{(d, W)} = \sum_{k=0}^{W-1} \omega_k X_{t-k}, \qquad \omega_0 = 1, \qquad \omega_k = -\omega_{k-1} \frac{d - k + 1}{k} \]

docs.title: 3. Modified Gram-Schmidt Cross-Sectional Orthogonalization
docs.text:
Applies the Frisch-Waugh-Lovell theorem per timestamp cross-section to strip collinear risk exposures \(F = [f_1, \dots, f_K]\) via sequential ridge-stabilized orthogonal projections:

\[ u_k = \tilde{f}_k - \sum_{j=1}^{k-1} \frac{\langle \tilde{f}_k, u_j \rangle}{\lVert u_j \rVert_2^2 + \lambda} u_j, \qquad \alpha_{\perp} = \tilde{\alpha} - \sum_{k=1}^{K} \frac{\langle \tilde{\alpha}, u_k \rangle}{\lVert u_k \rVert_2^2 + \lambda} u_k \]

docs.title: 4. Newey-West HAC Inference and Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR)
docs.text:
Corrects Rank IC \(t\)-statistics for overlapping forward-return serial correlation via Bartlett kernel variance \(\hat{\Omega}_{\text{NW}}\), and adjusts backtest Sharpe ratios for skewness (\(\hat{\gamma}_3\)), fat tails (\(\hat{\gamma}_4\)), and multiple testing across \(K\) trials:

\[ \hat{\Omega}_{\text{NW}} = \hat{\gamma}_0 + 2 \sum_{j=1}^{L} \left(1 - \frac{j}{L + 1}\right) \hat{\gamma}_j, \qquad \text{PSR}(\text{SR}^{\ast}) = \Phi\left(\frac{\widehat{\text{SR}} - \text{SR}^{\ast}}{\sqrt{\frac{1 - \hat{\gamma}_3 \widehat{\text{SR}} + \frac{\hat{\gamma}_4 - 1}{4}\widehat{\text{SR}}^2}{T - 1}}}\right) \]

docs.title: Architecture, Mathematical Reductions & Vectorization Engine
docs.text: polars-anta is engineered to bridge the gap between academic quantitative finance and production-grade systems engineering. Rather than wrapping legacy C libraries or iterating row-by-row in Python, every indicator, microstructure estimator, labeling algorithm, and backtesting primitive is formulated through closed-form algebraic identities, Apache Arrow zero-copy memory buffers, and Polars' multi-threaded Rust query engine.

docs.title: 1. Systems Architecture: Rust Engine, Apache Arrow & Rayon Parallelism
docs.text:
Traditional Python technical analysis libraries force quantitative researchers into an architectural trade-off:

Paradigm Representative Libraries Bottleneck in Research Workflows Compiled C Wrappers TA-Lib Requires native C toolchains (gcc / MSVC), breaks across Python ABI versions, operates only on 1D NumPy arrays, and cannot optimize multi-asset queries or lazy execution plans. Eager Pandas Wrappers pandas-ta, ta, alphalens Bound by Python's Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), copies memory eagerly on every intermediate Series operation, and executes groupby("symbol") sequentially on a single CPU core. Native Polars Expressions polars-anta Compiles indicators into a Polars Logical Plan, optimizes common subexpressions in Rust, executes across all CPU cores via Rayon work-stealing threads, and operates directly on Apache Arrow contiguous columnar buffers.

docs.title: Key Engineering Guarantees
docs.text:
1. Zero-Copy Arrow Buffers: Price, volume, and factor arrays are stored in 64-byte aligned contiguous memory blocks following the Apache Arrow specification, enabling AVX-256 / AVX-512 SIMD vectorization in Rust.
  2. Work-Stealing Multi-Asset Parallelism: When an expression is suffixed with .over("symbol") (time-series) or .over("timestamp") (cross-sectional), Polars dispatches independent partitions across all physical CPU cores concurrently via Rust's Rayon thread pool with zero Python callback serialization.
  3. Out-of-Core Streaming (pl.LazyFrame): Every method on TechnicalAnalysisFrame preserves lazy evaluation on pl.LazyFrame, allowing multi-year tick or 1-minute Parquet archives (pl.scan_parquet(...)) to be processed with minimal RAM footprint.

docs.title: 2. Closed-Form Algebraic Reductions (Mathematical Derivations)
docs.text: A core design principle of polars-anta is algebraic reduction: transforming seemingly \(O(N \cdot W)\) iterative regressions and recursive filters into \(O(N)\) native vectorized expressions.

docs.title: 2.1 Closed-Form Rolling OLS Linear Regression (112.4x Speedup)
docs.text:
In naive implementations (such as scipy.stats.linregress inside Series.rolling(n).apply(...)), computing a rolling Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) slope over a window of length \(n\) requires solving a regression at every bar \(t\), costing \(O(N \cdot n)\) in Python.

Theorem (WMA–SMA Decomposition of Rolling OLS): Let \(y_{t-n+1}, \dots, y_t\) be the \(n\) observations in the window ending at bar \(t\), indexed by local time \(x_i = i\) for \(i \in \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}\). The OLS linear model is \(y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_i + \epsilon_i\).

The sample mean of the time index is:

\[ \bar{x} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} i = \frac{n - 1}{2} \]

The sum of squared deviations of the time index is:

\[ S_{xx} = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (i - \bar{x})^2 = \frac{n(n^2 - 1)}{12} \]

Recall the definitions of the \(n\)-period Simple Moving Average (\(\text{SMA}_t\)) and Linearly Weighted Moving Average (\(\text{WMA}_t\)):

\[ \text{SMA}_t = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} y_{t - n + 1 + i}, \qquad \text{WMA}_t = \frac{2}{n(n + 1)} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (i + 1) y_{t - n + 1 + i} \]

Expanding the sample covariance \(S_{xy} = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (i - \bar{x}) y_{t - n + 1 + i}\):

\[ S_{xy} = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (i + 1) y_{t - n + 1 + i} - \frac{n + 1}{2} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} y_{t - n + 1 + i} = \frac{n(n + 1)}{2} \left( \text{WMA}_t - \text{SMA}_t \right) \]

Dividing \(S_{xy}\) by \(S_{xx}\) yields the exact closed-form identities implemented in polars_anta.stats:

\[ \hat{\beta}_1(t) = \frac{S_{xy}}{S_{xx}} = \frac{6}{n - 1} \left( \text{WMA}_t - \text{SMA}_t \right) \] \[ \hat{\beta}_0(t) = \text{SMA}_t - \hat{\beta}_1(t) \frac{n - 1}{2} = 4\,\text{SMA}_t - 3\,\text{WMA}_t \] \[ \hat{y}_t = \hat{\beta}_0(t) + \hat{\beta}_1(t)(n - 1) = 3\,\text{WMA}_t - 2\,\text{SMA}_t \]

Because both \(\text{SMA}_t\) and \(\text{WMA}_t\) execute natively in Rust, linear_regression_slope, linear_regression_intercept, and linear_regression_forecast evaluate 1,000,000 rows in 20.9 ms (112.4x faster than a pandas rolling().apply() baseline).

docs.title: 2.2 Exact Reduction of Recursive Filters to ewm_mean
docs.text:
Several classical indicators appear to require sequential bar-by-bar Python loops due to path-dependent recurrences:

  1. Wilder's Smoothing (RMA) used in rsi, atr, adx, and natr:
\[ \text{RMA}_t = \frac{(n - 1)\,\text{RMA}_{t-1} + x_t}{n} = \left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)\text{RMA}_{t-1} + \frac{1}{n} x_t \]

This is mathematically identical to an Exponential Moving Average with smoothing factor \(\alpha = \frac{1}{n}\) (or equivalent span \(S = 2n - 1\)), which maps directly to Polars' native C/Rust kernel expr.ewm_mean(alpha=1.0 / period, adjust=False, min_samples=period).

  1. Heikin-Ashi Synthetic Open (heikin_ashi): By definition, \(\text{Close}_t^{\text{HA}} = \frac{O_t + H_t + L_t + C_t}{4}\) and:
\[ \text{Open}_t^{\text{HA}} = \frac{1}{2}\text{Open}_{t-1}^{\text{HA}} + \frac{1}{2}\text{Close}_{t-1}^{\text{HA}} \]

Recognize that \(\text{Open}_t^{\text{HA}}\) is a first-order linear recurrence driven by the lagged input \(u_t = \text{Close}_{t-1}^{\text{HA}}\) with decay parameter \(\alpha = 0.5\) (span = 3). Thus, heikin_ashi computes the exact synthetic open across millions of rows in a single call to ha_close.shift(1).ewm_mean(alpha=0.5, adjust=False) with zero Python loops.

docs.title: 2.3 Modified Gram-Schmidt / Frisch-Waugh-Lovell Cross-Sectional Orthogonalization
docs.text:
In cross-sectional factor research, a candidate alpha \(Y\) must be orthogonalized against a vector of \(K\) continuous risk factors \(X = [X_1, X_2, \dots, X_K]\) (e.g., Market Beta, Volatility, Size, Amihud Illiquidity) at every cross-sectional timestamp \(t\).

Rather than grouping by timestamp in Python and invoking np.linalg.lstsq in a slow loop over \(T\) dates, orthogonalize applies the Frisch-Waugh-Lovell (FWL) Theorem via Modified Gram-Schmidt projections written entirely in native Polars .over(over) window expressions:

  1. Center the target signal and all risk factors within each cross-section \(t\):
\[ y^{(0)} = Y - \mathbb{E}_t[Y], \qquad u_j^{(0)} = X_j - \mathbb{E}_t[X_j] \quad (j = 1, \dots, K) \]
  1. For each orthogonal basis step \(j = 1, \dots, K\):
\[ q_j = u_j^{(j-1)}, \qquad \beta_{y, j} = \frac{\mathbb{E}_t\left[y^{(j-1)} q_j\right]}{\mathbb{E}_t\left[q_j^2\right] + \lambda} \] \[ y^{(j)} = y^{(j-1)} - \beta_{y, j} q_j \] \[ u_m^{(j)} = u_m^{(j-1)} - \frac{\mathbb{E}_t\left[u_m^{(j-1)} q_j\right]}{\mathbb{E}_t\left[q_j^2\right] + \lambda} q_j \quad \forall m > j \]
  1. After \(K\) symbolic steps, \(y^{(K)} = (I - P_X)(Y - \bar{Y})\) is the exact multivariate OLS residual satisfying \(\text{Corr}_t\left(y^{(K)}, X_j\right) = 0\) for all \(j = 1, \dots, K\), executed in parallel across all timestamps in Rust.

docs.title: 3. Zero-Copy Stride Kernels (sliding_window_view)
docs.text:
Certain financial machine learning and complexity primitives require inspecting the internal trajectory of a sliding window of length \(W\): - Fixed-Window Fractional Differentiation (frac_diff): Dot product of trailing window with binomial weights \(\omega_k\). - Triple-Barrier Labeling (triple_barrier_labels): First-passage time detection against upper Profit-Taking and lower Stop-Loss barriers over a forward window \(H\). - Rescaled Range Hurst Exponent (hurst_exponent): Cumulative demeaned range \(\max_{1 \le k \le W} Z_k - \min_{1 \le k \le W} Z_k\) within each window. - Shannon Entropy (entropy): Empirical histogram bin probabilities across each rolling window.

Instead of iterating over \(i \in \{0, \dots, N - W\}\) in Python, polars-anta uses NumPy's zero-copy stride manipulation: 

windows = np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(vals, window_shape=W)
Given a contiguous 1D float64 array of length \(N\) with byte stride \(s_0 = 8\) bytes, sliding_window_view constructs a 2D array descriptor of shape \((N - W + 1, W)\) and byte strides \((8, 8)\) in \(O(1)\) time with zero memory allocation. Matrix-vector products (windows @ w_rev in frac_diff) and vectorized boolean reductions (np.argmax(hit_pt, axis=1) in triple_barrier_labels) then execute directly in C/BLAS.

docs.title: 4. State-Machine Vectorization Without Loops
docs.text: Event-driven state machines are traditionally the hardest component to vectorize. polars-anta eliminates event loops across three critical domains:

docs.title: 4.1 Discrete Entry/Exit State Machine (signals_to_positions)
docs.text:
To hold \(+1.0\) from entries=True until exits=True (and \(-1.0\) for short triggers) without a bar-by-bar loop, polars-anta maps triggers to a tri-state sparse series:

\[ S_t = \begin{cases} 0.0 & \text{if } \text{Exit}_t \land \neg \text{Entry}_t \\ 1.0 & \text{if } \text{Entry}_t \\ \text{null} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Applying S_t.forward_fill().over("symbol").fill_null(0.0) propagates the active position state across time in \(O(N)\) native Rust execution.

docs.title: 4.2 Information-Driven Bar Sampling (resample_volume_bars, resample_dollar_bars, resample_imbalance_bars)
docs.text:
To group ticks or 1-minute bars into buckets whenever cumulative volume, dollar value, or signed tick imbalance crosses threshold \(\Theta\):

\[ B_t = \left\lfloor \frac{\left(\sum_{\tau=1}^{t} v_\tau\right) (1 - \epsilon)}{\Theta} \right\rfloor \]

Grouping by bar_id = B_t via Polars' group_by(["symbol", "bar_id"], maintain_order=True).agg(...) aggregates millions of ticks into Volume, Dollar, or Imbalance Bars in a single parallel pass.

docs.title: 4.3 Round-Trip Trade Ledger & Intra-Trade Excursion (extract_trades)
docs.text:
To extract individual round-trip trades and compute Maximum Adverse Excursion (MAE) and Maximum Favorable Excursion (MFE) without iterating over trades: 1. Detect state transitions where position sign changes: \(\text{seg}_t = \sum_{\tau=1}^{t} \mathbb{I}\left(\text{sign}(w_\tau) \neq \text{sign}(w_{\tau-1})\right)\). 2. Filter to active bars (\(w_t \neq 0\)) and compute intra-trade compounded gross return within each segment via window expression:

\[ G_t = \left(\prod_{\tau \in \text{seg}_t, \tau \le t} (1 + r_\tau^{\text{gross}})\right) - 1 \]
  1. Aggregate per seg_t in a single group_by pass:
\[ \text{MAE} = \min\left(0, \min_{t \in \text{seg}} G_t\right), \qquad \text{MFE} = \max\left(0, \max_{t \in \text{seg}} G_t\right) \]

docs.title: 1. Vectorized Linear Regression Decomposition
docs.text:
Traditional packages compute rolling linear regression by taking 1,000,000 windows and repeatedly solving \(y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 t\) with NumPy dot products.

polars-anta decomposes the OLS closed-form equation into Linearly Weighted Moving Average (WMA) and Simple Moving Average (SMA):

\[ \beta_1 = \frac{6}{N - 1} (\text{WMA} - \text{SMA}) \]

Because WMA and SMA execute in SIMD-vectorized Rust kernels, the rolling regression evaluates in 0.015 seconds instead of 1.80 seconds—over 116x faster!

docs.title: 2. Multi-Threaded Partitioning (.over())
docs.text: When processing multiple tickers, Polars automatically partitions data and distributes computation across all physical and logical CPU cores in Rust. Pandas .groupby().apply(), by contrast, iterates sequentially in a single Python thread.

docs.title: Guidelines for New Indicators
docs.text:
When adding a new indicator:

  1. Pure Expression First: Implement using pl.Expr wherever possible. Avoid Python loops over rows.
  2. Support String or Expr: Use parse_expr from polars_anta.core so users can pass either column names ("close") or existing expressions (pl.col("close")).
  3. Register on Dual Namespaces: Indicators added to TechnicalAnalysisExpr in polars_anta/namespace.py are automatically available under both .anta and .ta.
  4. Multi-Asset Compatibility: Ensure the indicator executes without errors inside .over("ticker").
  5. Structured Outputs: If the indicator produces multiple values (like bands or oscillators with signals), return a typed pl.Struct.
  6. Comprehensive Tests: Add test cases to the appropriate file in tests/. Verify test coverage remains above 90%: 
    pytest -v

docs.title: Core Paradigm: Expression-First
docs.text:
In Polars, computations are expressed as expressions (pl.Expr) rather than eager array modifications. This allows Polars to optimize queries, combine multiple operations into a single execution pass, and parallelize calculations across all CPU threads.

Importing polars_anta automatically attaches both .anta and .ta namespaces to Polars expressions:

import polars as pl
import polars_anta

docs.title: 1. Basic Calculation
docs.text:
Calculate indicators using .anta.<indicator>() (or .ta.<indicator>()) directly on columns:

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "open": [10.0, 10.5, 11.0, 10.8, 11.2],
        "high": [10.8, 11.2, 11.5, 11.1, 11.8],
        "low": [9.8, 10.2, 10.7, 10.5, 10.9],
        "close": [10.5, 11.0, 10.8, 11.2, 11.5],
        "volume": [1000, 1200, 950, 1100, 1500],
    }
)

result = df.with_columns(
    pl.col("close").anta.sma(3).alias("sma_3"),
    pl.col("close").anta.rsi(3).alias("rsi_3"),
    pl.col("close").anta.zscore(3).alias("zscore_3"),
)
print(result)

docs.title: 2. Multi-Component Struct Indicators
docs.text:
Indicators that output multiple components (like MACD, Bollinger Bands, Stochastic, Ichimoku) return a typed pl.Struct expression.

You can unpack all components into individual columns using .unnest():

# Compute Bollinger Bands
df_bands = df.with_columns(
    pl.col("close").anta.bollinger_bands(period=3, num_std=2.0).alias("bb")
).unnest("bb")

# Now columns `upper`, `middle`, `lower`, `bandwidth`, `percent_b` are directly available
print(df_bands.select(["close", "upper", "middle", "lower"]))

docs.title: 3. Functional Syntax
docs.text:
If you prefer functional import style, all indicators can also be imported directly from polars_anta:

from polars_anta import sma, rsi, bollinger_bands

result = df.with_columns(
    sma("close", period=3).alias("sma_3"),
    rsi("close", period=3).alias("rsi_3"),
    bollinger_bands("close", period=3).alias("bb"),
)

docs.title: 4. Fluent DataFrame & LazyFrame Chaining
docs.text:
In addition to expression-level calls, polars-anta provides direct DataFrame and LazyFrame chaining via .anta and .ta:

import polars as pl
import polars_anta

# Validate data, resample, and chain indicators directly:
features = (
    df.anta.validate_ohlcv()
    .anta.resample("15m", group_by="symbol")
    .anta.sma(20)
    .anta.rsi(14)
    .anta.macd(unnest=True)
    .anta.bollinger_bands(unnest=True)
)

# Or batch generate a complete feature suite:
all_features = df.anta.add_all(group_by="symbol")

docs.title: Parallel Multi-Asset & Cross-Sectional Scaling with .over()
docs.text:
In quantitative research, a pipeline operates simultaneously along two orthogonal axes of a panel dataset \((i \in \{1, \dots, N_{\text{assets}}\},\; t \in \{1, \dots, T_{\text{bars}}\})\):

  1. Time-Series Axis (.over("symbol")): Rolling moving averages, fractional differentiation (frac_diff), volatility estimators (garman_klass_volatility), and path-dependent labels (triple_barrier_labels) computed independently per instrument across time.
  2. Cross-Sectional Axis (.over("timestamp")): Winsorization (cs_winsorize), standardization (cs_zscore), sector neutralization (neutralize), and multi-factor OLS orthogonalization (orthogonalize) computed across all instruments at each point in time.

docs.title: Combining Time-Series & Cross-Sectional Expressions in One Query
docs.text:
Because every polars-anta indicator is a native pl.Expr, Polars' query optimizer fuses both time-series .over("symbol") and cross-sectional .over("timestamp") operations into a single parallel execution graph:

import polars as pl
import polars_anta as pa

panel_alpha = (
    universe_df.with_columns(
        [
            # Step 1: Time-series features partitioned per asset (.over("symbol"))
            pl.col("close").anta.frac_diff(d=0.4, window=20).over("symbol").alias("ffd_04"),
            pa.garman_klass_volatility("open", "high", "low", "close", period=20)
            .over("symbol")
            .alias("gk_vol"),
            pa.amihud_illiquidity("close", "volume", period=20).over("symbol").alias("amihud"),
            pl.col("close").anta.roc(10).over("symbol").alias("mom_10"),
        ]
    )
    .with_columns(
        [
            # Step 2: Cross-sectional outlier clipping & standardization per timestamp
            pl.col("mom_10")
            .anta.cs_winsorize(over="timestamp", method="mad", threshold=3.0)
            .anta.cs_zscore(over="timestamp")
            .alias("mom_z"),
        ]
    )
    .with_columns(
        [
            # Step 3: Cross-sectional Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization against risk factors
            pl.col("mom_z")
            .anta.orthogonalize(
                factors=["gk_vol", "amihud"],
                over="timestamp",
                standardize=True,
            )
            .alias("ortho_alpha"),
        ]
    )
)

docs.title: Why .over() Outperforms Pandas groupby by 8x–112x
docs.text:
1. Rayon Work-Stealing Thread Pool: Polars partitions the hash table of "symbol" or "timestamp" and distributes disjoint index slices across all CPU cores in Rust without acquiring Python's GIL.
  2. Cache-Local Arrow Slices: Group operations read contiguous 64-byte aligned Arrow arrays rather than allocating a new Python pd.DataFrame object per ticker.
  3. Expression Graph Fusion: Multiple .over("symbol") expressions inside the same .with_columns([...]) block share the same group partition index map, computing the partition hash only once.

docs.title: Quantitative Theory & End-to-End Workflows
docs.text:
This guide presents the quantitative finance theory, mathematical formulations, and production Polars implementations across the four core pillars of alpha research in polars-anta:

  1. Pillar 1 — Derivatives & Intraday Market Microstructure: Information-driven bar sampling, adverse selection & order flow toxicity (VPIN, OFI), session-anchored VWAP, index futures cost-of-carry basis, open interest regime classification, and continuous contract roll stitching.
  2. Pillar 2 — Quantitative Machine Learning (AFML Primitives): Memory-preserving stationarity via Fixed-Window Fractional Differentiation (FFD), dynamic Triple-Barrier labeling, Meta-Labeling, and multi-horizon OLS Trend-Scanning.
  3. Pillar 3 — Factor Validation & Risk Orthogonalization: Cross-sectional preprocessing, Frisch-Waugh-Lovell multi-factor orthogonalization, Newey-West HAC \(t\)-statistics, Information Coefficient (IC) decay & Alpha Half-Life, and multiple-testing adjustments (Probabilistic & Deflated Sharpe Ratio).
  4. Pillar 4 — Execution-Realistic Backtesting & Excursion Analytics: Next-Open / TWAP / VWAP execution models, intraday EOD session flattening, dynamic Volatility Targeting, no-trade turnover buffers, and Round-Trip Trade Ledgers with Maximum Adverse/Favorable Excursion (MAE/MFE).

docs.title: 1.1 Why Chronological Time Bars Fail in Intraday Markets
docs.text:
Standard chronological bars (e.g., 1-minute or 5-minute candles) sample the market at fixed wall-clock intervals regardless of trading activity. During quiet midday sessions, time bars oversample microstructure noise; during market open, macro announcements, or ATC auctions (such as on the VN30F1M index futures market), time bars undersample rapid price discovery. Consequently, time-sampled returns exhibit severe serial correlation, heteroskedasticity, and leptokurtic fat tails (Clark, 1973; López de Prado, 2018).

Information-Driven Bars synchronize sampling with the arrival of market activity:

  • Volume Bars (resample_volume_bars): Emit a new bar whenever cumulative traded contracts/shares reach threshold \(\Theta_V\):
\[ b_t^{(V)} = \left\lfloor \frac{\sum_{\tau=1}^t V_\tau}{\Theta_V} \right\rfloor \]
  • Dollar / Notional Bars (resample_dollar_bars): Emit a new bar whenever cumulative notional value \(\sum_{\tau=1}^t P_\tau V_\tau\) crosses \(\Theta_D\). Dollar bars automatically adapt to large secular price changes or inflation.
  • Volume / Tick Imbalance Bars (resample_imbalance_bars): Let \(s_t = \text{sign}(\Delta P_t) \in \{-1, +1\}\) (propagated forward via the Lee-Ready tick rule when \(\Delta P_t = 0\)). The signed flow is \(\theta_t = s_t V_t\) (or \(s_t\) for tick imbalance). A new bar is emitted whenever cumulative directional imbalance since the previous bar reset exceeds \(\Theta_{\text{imb}}\):
\[ \left| \sum_{\tau = t_0}^t \theta_\tau \right| \ge \Theta_{\text{imb}} \]

Quantitative Property: Restoration of Return Normality

Empirically across equity index futures (E-mini S&P 500, VN30F1M), sampling in Volume or Dollar time subordinate to the trading clock (Ané & Geman, 2000) restores return distributions much closer to i.i.d. Gaussianity, significantly improving the stability of GARCH, Kalman filter, and gradient-boosted tree models.

import polars as pl
import polars_anta as pa

# Convert 1-minute or tick data into 5,000-contract Volume Bars & Imbalance Bars
vol_bars = df.anta.resample_volume_bars(threshold=5_000, group_by="symbol")
imb_bars = df.anta.resample_imbalance_bars(threshold=1_500, mode="volume", group_by="symbol")

docs.title: 1.2 Order Flow Toxicity & Adverse Selection: VPIN & OFI
docs.text: Market makers and algorithmic execution desks face adverse selection risk when trading against informed institutional flow.

docs.title: Bulk Volume Classification VPIN (vpin)
docs.text:
Following Easley, López de Prado & O'Hara (2012), when tick-by-tick trade aggressor flags are unavailable or noisy, bar volume \(V_t\) is partitioned into buyer-initiated (\(V_t^B\)) and seller-initiated (\(V_t^S\)) components using the standardized price change \(Z_t = \frac{\Delta P_t}{\sigma_{\Delta P}}\):

\[ V_t^B = V_t \cdot \Phi\left(\frac{\Delta P_t}{\sigma_{\Delta P}}\right), \qquad V_t^S = V_t - V_t^B \]

In polars-anta, \(\Phi(z)\) is approximated via the smooth sigmoid \(\left(1 + \exp(-1.702\,z)\right)^{-1}\) (which matches the standard normal CDF within \(0.0095\) uniformly across \(\mathbb{R}\)). The Volume-Synchronized Probability of Informed Trading over window \(N\) is:

\[ \text{VPIN}_t = \frac{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \left| V_{t-k}^B - V_{t-k}^S \right|}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} V_{t-k}} \in [0, 1] \]

docs.title: Order Flow Imbalance (ofi)
docs.text:
Following Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov (2014), short-horizon price changes are linearly driven by net supply/demand shifts at the best bid (\(P_t^B, Q_t^B\)) and best ask (\(P_t^A, Q_t^A\)):

\[ e_t^B = Q_t^B \mathbb{I}_{\{P_t^B \ge P_{t-1}^B\}} - Q_{t-1}^B \mathbb{I}_{\{P_t^B \le P_{t-1}^B\}} \] \[ e_t^A = Q_t^A \mathbb{I}_{\{P_t^A \le P_{t-1}^A\}} - Q_{t-1}^A \mathbb{I}_{\{P_t^A \ge P_{t-1}^A\}} \] \[ \text{OFI}_t(N) = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \left( e_{t-k}^B - e_{t-k}^A \right) \]

docs.title: 1.3 Index Futures Cost-of-Carry, Open Interest Regimes & Continuous Roll Stitching
Futures Basis (futures_basis)
docs.text:
By no-arbitrage pricing, an index futures contract \(F_t\) maturing at \(T\) is linked to the underlying spot index \(S_t\) (e.g., VN30F1M vs. VN30 cash index) by the cost-of-carry relation \(F_t = S_t e^{(r - q)\tau}\). futures_basis computes:

\[ \text{Basis}_t = F_t - S_t, \qquad \text{Basis\%}_t = \frac{F_t - S_t}{S_t}, \qquad \text{Carry}_{\text{ann}, t} = \frac{F_t - S_t}{S_t} \cdot \frac{365}{\max(\text{DTE}_t, 1)} \]

along with the rolling standardized anomaly score \(\text{ZScore}(\text{Basis}_t, N)\) for index arbitrage and cash-and-carry strategies.

docs.title: Open Interest 4-Phase Regime Classification (oi_regime)
docs.text:
Combining price change \(\Delta P_t = P_t - P_{t-k}\) and Open Interest change \(\Delta \text{OI}_t = \text{OI}_t - \text{OI}_{t-k}\) classifies futures market participation into four regimes:

Price \(\Delta P_t\) Open Interest \(\Delta \text{OI}_t\) Regime Code Interpretation \(> 0\) \(> 0\) +2.0 Long Buildup: Fresh long positions opening; strong bullish trend conviction. \(> 0\) \(< 0\) +1.0 Short Covering: Rally driven by shorts buying back to close; weaker follow-through. \(< 0\) \(> 0\) -2.0 Short Buildup: Fresh short positions opening; strong bearish conviction. \(< 0\) \(< 0\) -1.0 Long Liquidation: Decline driven by existing longs forced to exit/deleverage.

docs.title: Continuous Futures Roll Stitching (stitch_futures_roll)
docs.text: When a front-month futures contract expires and rolls into the next maturity (contract changes from \(C_k\) to \(C_{k+1}\)), raw price series exhibit artificial price jumps \(\Delta_{\text{roll}} = P_{t, \text{new}}^{\text{open}} - P_{t-1, \text{old}}^{\text{close}}\) that corrupt moving averages, RSI, and backtest returns. stitch_futures_roll supports three adjustment modes: 1. method="panama" (Additive Backward/Forward Adjustment): Preserves exact point/tick differences \(\Delta P_t\) and point PnL by shifting historical contracts by the cumulative roll gap. 2. method="ratio" (Multiplicative Adjustment): Preserves exact percentage returns \(r_t = P_t / P_{t-1} - 1\) across contract rolls by scaling prices by the cumulative roll ratio \(\prod (P_{\text{new}} / P_{\text{old}})\).

docs.title: 2.1 The Stationarity vs. Memory Dilemma: Fractional Differentiation (frac_diff)
docs.text:
Raw log-prices \(p_t = \ln P_t\) are non-stationary (\(I(1)\)), violating the i.i.d. assumptions of supervised machine learning estimators. However, taking first differences \(\Delta p_t = (1 - B) p_t\) (\(d = 1\)) completely wipes out long-term trend and support/resistance memory.

Following López de Prado (2018, Chapter 5), the fractional differencing operator \((1 - B)^d\) for real order \(d \in (0, 1)\) expands via the generalized binomial series:

\[ (1 - B)^d = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \binom{d}{k} (-B)^k = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \omega_k B^k \]

where the weights satisfy the exact recurrence:

\[ \omega_0 = 1, \qquad \omega_k = -\omega_{k-1} \frac{d - k + 1}{k} \quad (k \ge 1) \]

In Fixed-Window Fractional Differentiation (FFD), the filter is truncated at a fixed lookback window \(W\):

\[ \tilde{X}_t^{(d, W)} = \sum_{k=0}^{W-1} \omega_k X_{t-k} \]

Typically, \(d \in [0.3, 0.5]\) achieves statistical stationarity (passing the Augmented Dickey-Fuller test) while retaining \(> 90\%\) correlation with the original price level.

docs.title: 2.2 Dynamic Triple-Barrier Labeling & Meta-Labeling (triple_barrier_labels)
docs.text:
Fixed-horizon return labels \(y_t = \text{sign}(P_{t+H} / P_t - 1)\) are flawed because they ignore the path taken by price between \(t\) and \(t+H\) (a position would have been stopped out intra-horizon) and use a static threshold regardless of volatility regimes.

triple_barrier_labels constructs three dynamic barriers for each bar \(t\) based on local volatility \(\sigma_t\): 1. Upper Profit-Taking (PT) Barrier: \(U_t = +\max\left(m_{\text{PT}} \cdot \sigma_t,\, r_{\min}\right)\) 2. Lower Stop-Loss (SL) Barrier: \(L_t = -\max\left(m_{\text{SL}} \cdot \sigma_t,\, r_{\min}\right)\) 3. Vertical Expiration Barrier: \(t + H\) bars.

Let \(\tau_{\text{PT}} = \min\{k \in \{1, \dots, H\} : r_{t, t+k}^{\text{dir}} \ge U_t\}\) and \(\tau_{\text{SL}} = \min\{k \in \{1, \dots, H\} : r_{t, t+k}^{\text{dir}} \le L_t\}\). The first touched barrier determines: - label: \(+1.0\) (upper barrier hit first), \(-1.0\) (lower barrier hit first), or \(0.0\) (vertical horizon expired first). - touch_bars: First-passage time \(\tau = \min(\tau_{\text{PT}}, \tau_{\text{SL}}, H) \in \{1, \dots, H\}\). - realized_return: Raw return \((P_{t + \tau} - P_t) / P_t\) at the barrier touch. - meta_label: Binary \(\{0.0, 1.0\}\) indicating whether the primary directional signal side (\(\in \{-1, +1\}\)) achieved its profit-taking target.

docs.title: 2.3 Multi-Horizon Trend-Scanning Labels (trend_scanning_labels)
docs.text:
Proposed by López de Prado (2020, Machine Learning for Asset Managers), Trend-Scanning eliminates arbitrary fixed lookahead horizons by fitting forward OLS regressions across a grid of candidate horizons \(L \in [L_{\min}, L_{\max}]\):

\[ P_{t+i} = \beta_0(L) + \beta_1(L) \cdot i + \epsilon_i, \qquad i = 0, 1, \dots, L - 1 \]

For each candidate window \(L\), the slope \(t\)-statistic is:

\[ t_{\hat{\beta}_1}(L) = \frac{\hat{\beta}_1(L)}{\text{SE}(\hat{\beta}_1(L))}, \qquad \text{SE}(\hat{\beta}_1(L)) = \sqrt{\frac{\text{SSR}(L) / (L - 2)}{S_{xx}(L)}} \]

trend_scanning_labels selects the optimal horizon \(L^*_t = \arg\max_{L} \left|t_{\hat{\beta}_1}(L)\right|\) using closed-form Polars expressions and returns Struct(label, t_value, optimal_window, ret).

docs.title: 3.1 Newey-West HAC \(t\)-Statistics & Multi-Horizon IC Decay (ic_summary, ic_decay)
docs.text:
When evaluating an alpha factor against \(h\)-period forward returns (\(h > 1\)), overlapping return windows induce Moving Average \(\text{MA}(h - 1)\) serial correlation in the cross-sectional Information Coefficient series \(\{\text{IC}_t\}_{t=1}^T\). Standard i.i.d. \(t\)-statistics \(\frac{\overline{\text{IC}}}{\hat{\sigma}_{\text{IC}} / \sqrt{T}}\) severely overstate statistical significance.

ic_summary computes the Newey-West (1987) Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent (HAC) long-run variance estimator using the Bartlett kernel up to lag \(L\):

\[ \hat{\Omega}_{\text{NW}} = \hat{\gamma}_0 + 2 \sum_{j=1}^{L} \left(1 - \frac{j}{L + 1}\right) \hat{\gamma}_j, \qquad \hat{\gamma}_j = \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=j+1}^{T} (\text{IC}_t - \overline{\text{IC}})(\text{IC}_{t-j} - \overline{\text{IC}}) \] \[ t_{\text{NW}} = \frac{\overline{\text{IC}}}{\sqrt{\hat{\Omega}_{\text{NW}} / T}} \]

ic_decay evaluates ic_summary across a vector of forward horizons \(h \in (1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20)\) (automatically setting nw_lags = max(1, h - 1)) and estimates the Alpha Half-Life via log-linear regression \(\ln |\overline{\text{IC}}(h)| = a - \lambda h \implies t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\hat{\lambda}}\).

docs.title: 3.2 Correcting Backtest Overfitting: Probabilistic & Deflated Sharpe Ratio
docs.text: Standard Sharpe Ratio estimates ignore non-normality (negative skewness and excess kurtosis inflate tail risk) and multiple-testing selection bias (running \(N\) parameter combinations guarantees finding a high in-sample Sharpe by chance).

docs.title: Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio (probabilistic_sharpe_ratio — Bailey & López de Prado, 2012)
docs.text:
Given sample size \(T\), non-annualized Sharpe \(\widehat{SR}\), skewness \(\hat{\gamma}_3\), and Pearson kurtosis \(\hat{\gamma}_4\), the asymptotic standard error of \(\widehat{SR}\) is:

\[ \hat{\sigma}(\widehat{SR}) = \sqrt{\frac{1 - \hat{\gamma}_3 \widehat{SR} + \frac{\hat{\gamma}_4 - 1}{4} \widehat{SR}^2}{T - 1}} \]

The probability that the true Sharpe ratio exceeds benchmark \(\text{SR}^{\ast}\) is:

\[ \text{PSR}(\text{SR}^{\ast}) = \Phi\left(\frac{\widehat{\text{SR}} - \text{SR}^{\ast}}{\hat{\sigma}(\widehat{\text{SR}})}\right) \in [0, 1] \]

docs.title: Deflated Sharpe Ratio (deflated_sharpe_ratio — Bailey & López de Prado, 2014)
docs.text:
When a researcher selects the best strategy out of \(N\) independent trials (n_trials) whose annualized Sharpe ratios have standard deviation \(\sigma_{\{SR\}}\), Extreme Value Theory (False Strategy Theorem) gives the expected maximum annualized Sharpe ratio under the null hypothesis of zero skill:

\[ \text{SR}^{\ast}_{\text{ann}}(N) = \sigma_{\{SR\}} \left[ (1 - \gamma) \Phi^{-1}\left(1 - \frac{1}{N}\right) + \gamma \Phi^{-1}\left(1 - \frac{1}{N \cdot e}\right) \right] \]

where \(\gamma \approx 0.5772156649\) is the Euler-Mascheroni constant. Plugging \(\text{SR}^{\ast}_{\text{ann}}(N)\) into \(\text{PSR}(\text{SR}^{\ast})\) yields the Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR). A common threshold is \(\text{DSR} \ge 0.95\).

docs.title: Pillar 4: Execution-Realistic Backtesting & Excursion Analytics
docs.text:
vectorized_backtest (df.anta.backtest) extends vectorized simulation with four execution controls and a full Round-Trip Trade Ledger:

bt = df.anta.backtest(
    signal="alpha_signal",
    execution_price="open",  # Execute at next bar's Open (or 'twap' / 'vwap')
    flat_mask=pl.col("time") >= "14:25:00",  # Force 0 position at intraday EOD session close
    vol_target=0.15,  # 15% annualized dynamic volatility targeting
    vol_lookback=20,
    max_leverage=2.0,
    no_trade_buffer=0.05,  # Suppress tiny rebalances < 5% weight change
    fee_rate=0.0003,
    slippage_rate=0.0002,
)

# Inspect tearsheet and Round-Trip Trade Ledger with MAE / MFE
print(bt.report())
print(bt.trades())

docs.title: Interpreting MAE & MFE in bt.trades()
docs.text: For every closed round-trip trade \(k\), bt.trades() reports: - mae (Maximum Adverse Excursion \(\le 0\)): The worst intra-trade drawdown from entry price experienced before the trade closed. If winning trades consistently have \(\text{MAE} > -1.2\%\), placing a hard stop-loss at \(-1.5\%\) cuts tail losses without prematurely stopping out winners. - mfe (Maximum Favorable Excursion \(\ge 0\)): The highest unrealized profit reached during the trade's lifetime. Comparing mfe against final gross_return reveals how much profit is given back before exit.

docs.title: Time Bars, Information-Driven Bars & Continuous Futures Roll (polars_anta.resample)
docs.text:
In quantitative workflows, raw market feeds (tick data, Level-1 order book updates, or 1-minute candles) must be validated, stitched across futures contract expirations, and aggregated into chronological or activity-driven bars before feature extraction.

polars-anta provides six native Polars data engineering primitives in polars_anta.resample:

  1. resample_ohlcv: Chronological multi-timeframe aggregation ("5m", "15m", "1h", "1d") via Polars' group_by_dynamic.
  2. resample_volume_bars: Activity-synchronized Volume Bars emitted every \(\Theta_V\) traded contracts/shares.
  3. resample_dollar_bars: Notional-synchronized Dollar Bars emitted every \(\Theta_D\) currency value traded.
  4. resample_imbalance_bars: Order-flow-synchronized Tick / Volume Imbalance Bars (AFML) emitted whenever signed directional flow exceeds \(\Theta_{\text{imb}}\).
  5. stitch_futures_roll: Continuous futures contract splicing via additive ("panama"), multiplicative ("ratio"), or unadjusted ("none") roll adjustment.
  6. validate_ohlcv: High-speed structural integrity verification (High >= Low, non-negative prices, monotonic timestamps).

docs.title: resample_volume_bars(df, threshold, ...) & resample_dollar_bars(df, threshold, ...)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation: Let \(v_t = V_t\) for Volume Bars, or \(v_t = C_t \cdot V_t\) for Dollar Bars. The cumulative activity bucket index is:

\[ b_t = \left\lfloor \frac{\left(\sum_{\tau=1}^t v_\tau\right)(1 - \epsilon)}{\Theta} \right\rfloor \]

Grouping by bar_id = b_t aggregates standard OHLCV columns along with tick_count (number of raw observations merged into the bar) and vwap (\(\sum C_\tau V_\tau / \sum V_\tau\)).

import polars_anta as pa

# Aggregate 1-minute VN30F1M bars into 5,000-contract Volume Bars
vol_bars = df.anta.resample_volume_bars(threshold=5_000, group_by="symbol")

# Aggregate into 500 Billion VND Notional Dollar Bars
dollar_bars = df.anta.resample_dollar_bars(threshold=5e11, group_by="symbol")

docs.title: resample_imbalance_bars(df, threshold, mode="volume", ...)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation (López de Prado, 2018): Using the Lee-Ready tick rule \(s_t = \text{sign}(C_t - C_{t-1})\) (forward-filled when \(\Delta C_t = 0\)), let signed flow be \(\theta_t = s_t V_t\) (mode="volume") or \(\theta_t = s_t\) (mode="tick"). A new bar is triggered at bar \(t\) whenever cumulative imbalance since the start of the current bar \(t_0\) crosses threshold:

\[ \left| \sum_{\tau = t_0}^t \theta_\tau \right| \ge \Theta_{\text{imb}} \]

Each output bar includes bar_id, open, high, low, close, volume, imbalance (\(\sum_{\tau=t_0}^t \theta_\tau\)), tick_count, and vwap.

docs.title: stitch_futures_roll(df, contract_col="contract", method="panama", backward=True, ...)
docs.text:
When constructing multi-year historical series for index futures (e.g., splicing VN30F2601 \(\to\) VN30F2602 \(\to\) VN30F2603), contract switches create artificial price gaps \(\delta_k = O_{t_k, \text{new}} - C_{t_k - 1, \text{old}}\) at roll timestamps \(t_k\).

Method Mathematical Adjustment (backward=True, anchoring latest contract to actual market price) Preserved Invariant method="panama" \(P_{t}^{\text{adj}} = P_t + \sum_{t_k > t} \left(O_{t_k, \text{new}} - C_{t_k - 1, \text{old}}\right)\) Preserves exact point differences (\(\Delta P_t\)) and point-based ATR / stop distances. method="ratio" \(P_{t}^{\text{adj}} = P_t \times \prod_{t_k > t} \left(\frac{O_{t_k, \text{new}}}{C_{t_k - 1, \text{old}}}\right)\) Preserves exact percentage returns (\(r_t\)) and keeps historical prices strictly positive. method="none" \(P_t^{\text{adj}} = P_t\) Appends roll_flag and roll_adjustment columns for inspection without modifying OHLC. 
continuous_df = df.anta.stitch_futures_roll(
    contract_col="contract",
    method="panama",
    backward=True,
    group_by="underlying",
)

docs.title: 3. Chronological Multi-Timeframe Resampling (resample_ohlcv)
docs.text:
# Resample 1-minute multi-asset universe to 15-minute bars in parallel
df_15m = df.anta.resample(
    every="15m",
    group_by="symbol",
    time_col="timestamp",
    additional_aggs=[pl.col("open_interest").last().alias("open_interest")],
)

docs.title: 4. Structural Integrity Validation (validate_ohlcv)
docs.text: Before training ML models or running backtests, validate_ohlcv checks four structural invariants in a single vectorized pass: 1. Schema & Types: Price/volume columns are numeric; timestamp is pl.Date or pl.Datetime. 2. OHLC Envelope: \(H_t \ge \max(O_t, C_t, L_t)\) and \(L_t \le \min(O_t, C_t, H_t)\). 3. Positivity: Prices are strictly positive (\(> 0\)) and volume is non-negative (\(\ge 0\)). 4. Temporal Ordering: No null timestamps and strictly non-decreasing timestamps within each group_by partition.

docs.title: Three Interchangeable Invocation Patterns
docs.text:
Every indicator and quantitative primitive in polars-anta can be called via three equivalent interfaces:

import polars as pl
import polars_anta as pa  # Registers .anta and .ta on Expr, DataFrame, and LazyFrame

# 1. Expression Namespace (.anta or .ta) — composable inside .select() / .with_columns()
df = df.with_columns(
    pl.col("close").anta.frac_diff(d=0.4, window=20).over("symbol").alias("close_ffd"),
    pl.col("close").ta.rsi(14).over("symbol").alias("rsi_14"),
)

# 2. DataFrame / LazyFrame Fluent Chaining — end-to-end research & backtesting pipelines
bt = (
    df.anta.validate_ohlcv(group_by="symbol")
    .anta.session_vwap(unnest=True, group_by="symbol")
    .anta.rsi(14, group_by="symbol")
    .anta.backtest(
        entries=pl.col("rsi_14").anta.crosses_above(30, over="symbol"),
        exits=pl.col("rsi_14").anta.crosses_below(70, over="symbol"),
        execution_price="open",
        vol_target=0.15,
        fee_rate=0.0005,
    )
)

# 3. Direct Functional Import — explicit top-level calls
decay_table = pa.ic_decay(df, factor_col="close_ffd", asset_col="symbol", group_by="timestamp")

docs.title: Alpha Factor, Microstructure & Derivatives Primitives (polars_anta.alpha)
docs.text: The polars_anta.alpha module provides 71 alpha primitives spanning cross-sectional standardization and multi-factor OLS orthogonalization, order flow toxicity (VPIN, OFI), index futures basis & open interest regimes, liquidity/spread estimators, fractal complexity metrics, and 33 canonical formulaic alphas.

docs.title: 1. Cross-Sectional Standardization, Neutralization & Orthogonalization
docs.text:
In multi-asset quantitative equity and futures portfolios, raw signals must be cleaned of outliers, standardized across the cross-section at each timestamp \(t\), and orthogonalized against systematic risk factors.

flowchart LR
    R["Raw Alpha Signal<br/>alpha_raw"] --> W["1. Outlier Clipping<br/>cs_winsorize(method='mad')"]
    W --> Z["2. Standardization<br/>cs_zscore(clip_bound=3.0)"]
    Z --> N["3. Sector Demeaning<br/>neutralize(by='sector')"]
    N --> O["4. Risk Orthogonalization<br/>orthogonalize(['beta', 'vol'])"]
    O --> S["5. Book Sizing<br/>ts_scale(a=1.0)"]

docs.title: cs_rank(expr, over=None, method="average", percentile=True)
docs.text:
Computes the cross-sectional rank across all assets at each timestamp over:

\[ \text{CSRank}_{i, t} = \frac{\text{rank}(x_{i, t})}{N_t} \in \left(\frac{1}{N_t}, 1.0\right] \]

Transforms arbitrary skewed cross-sectional distributions into a uniform distribution, ensuring extreme outliers cannot dominate portfolio weights.

docs.title: cs_zscore(expr, over=None, clip_bound=None)
docs.text:
Cross-sectional zero-mean, unit-variance standardization at each timestamp \(t\):

\[ Z_{i, t} = \frac{x_{i, t} - \mu_t}{\sigma_t}, \qquad \mu_t = \frac{1}{N_t}\sum_{j=1}^{N_t} x_{j, t} \]

When clip_bound is specified (e.g., clip_bound=3.0), clips \(Z_{i, t}\) into \([-c, +c]\) where \(c\) is clip_bound.

docs.title: cs_winsorize(expr, over=None, method="quantile", lower=0.01, upper=0.99, threshold=3.0)
docs.text: Cross-sectional outlier clipping within each timestamp over supporting three statistical estimators: - method="quantile": Clips values outside empirical quantiles \([Q_{\text{lower}}, Q_{\text{upper}}]\). - method="zscore": Clips values outside \([\mu_t - k\sigma_t,\, \mu_t + k\sigma_t]\) where \(k = \text{threshold}\). - method="mad" (Robust Median Absolute Deviation): Uses the consistent normal-equivalent MAD scale \(\hat{\sigma}_{\text{MAD}} = 1.4826 \cdot \text{ median}(|x_{i,t} - \text{median}_t|)\) and clips outside \([\text{median}_t - k\hat{\sigma}_{\text{MAD}},\, \text{median}_t + k\hat{\sigma}_{\text{MAD}}]\).

docs.title: neutralize(expr, by, over=None, standardize=False)
docs.text:
Categorical Group / Sector / Industry Neutralization (WorldQuant primitive indneutralize(x, g)):

\[ \tilde{x}_{i, t} = x_{i, t} - \frac{1}{|G(i)|} \sum_{j \in G(i)} x_{j, t} \]

Ensures that the sum of long and short weights within every sector \(G\) at every timestamp \(t\) is strictly zero (\(\sum_{i \in G} \tilde{x}_{i, t} = 0\)).

docs.title: orthogonalize(expr, factors, over=None, standardize=True, ridge=0.0)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell / Modified Gram-Schmidt OLS Projection): Given target alpha signal \(Y\) and continuous risk exposures \(X = [X_1, \dots, X_K]\) (such as Market Beta, Volatility, Size, or Amihud Illiquidity), orthogonalize removes all linear exposure to \(\text{span}(1, X_1, \dots, X_K)\) within each cross-section over:

\[ \epsilon_t = (I - P_{X_t})(Y_t - \bar{Y}_t) \implies \text{Corr}_t(\epsilon_t, X_{j, t}) = 0 \quad \forall j \in \{1, \dots, K\} \]
  • Quantitative Theory: Whereas neutralize handles discrete categorical buckets (sectors), orthogonalize handles continuous risk factors. By applying iterated Modified Gram-Schmidt projections in pure Polars .over(over) window expressions, the resulting residual \(\epsilon_t\) represents pure idiosyncratic alpha orthogonal to all specified risk factors.
  • Example: 
    df = df.anta.orthogonalize(
    col="raw_alpha",
    factors=["market_beta", "realized_vol", "amihud_20"],
    over="date",
    standardize=True,
    alias="pure_alpha",
)

docs.title: ts_scale(expr, a=1.0, over=None)
docs.text:
L1 Book-Size Normalization (WorldQuant primitive scale(x, a)):

\[ w_{i, t} = \frac{a \cdot x_{i, t}}{\sum_{j=1}^{N_t} |x_{j, t}|} \implies \sum_{i=1}^{N_t} |w_{i, t}| = a \]

docs.title: 2. Intraday Order Flow, Microstructure & Liquidity Estimators
vpin(close, volume, period=20)
docs.text:
Bulk Volume Classification (BVC) Volume-Synchronized Probability of Informed Trading (Easley, López de Prado & O'Hara, 2012):

\[ V_t^B = V_t \cdot \Phi\left(\frac{\Delta P_t}{\hat{\sigma}_{\Delta P, t}}\right), \qquad V_t^S = V_t - V_t^B, \qquad \text{VPIN}_t = \frac{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} |V_{t-k}^B - V_{t-k}^S|}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} V_{t-k}} \in [0, 1] \]

Measures order flow toxicity and adverse selection risk without requiring tick-level trade direction flags. Elevated VPIN values warn of informed institutional order flow and impending volatility expansion.

docs.title: ofi(bid_price, bid_size, ask_price, ask_size, period=1)
docs.text:
Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov (2014) Level-1 Order Flow Imbalance:

\[ e_t^B = q_t^B \mathbb{I}_{\{b_t \ge b_{t-1}\}} - q_{t-1}^B \mathbb{I}_{\{b_t \le b_{t-1}\}}, \qquad e_t^A = q_t^A \mathbb{I}_{\{a_t \le a_{t-1}\}} - q_{t-1}^A \mathbb{I}_{\{a_t \ge a_{t-1}\}} \] \[ \text{OFI}_t(N) = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \left(e_{t-k}^B - e_{t-k}^A\right) \]

Quantifies net limit order book supply/demand pressure at the best bid and ask queues.

docs.title: amihud_illiquidity(close, volume, period=20, scale=1e6)
docs.text:
Amihud (2002) Price-Impact Illiquidity Ratio:

\[ \text{ILLIQ}_t = \frac{\text{scale}}{N} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \frac{|r_{t-k}|}{P_{t-k} \cdot V_{t-k}} \]

Measures the average absolute percentage price impact per unit of dollar volume traded.

docs.title: roll_spread(close, period=20) & corwin_schultz_spread(high, low, period=20)
docs.text:
• Roll (1984) Implicit Bid-Ask Spread: Estimates effective spread from first-order negative serial covariance of log price changes caused by bid-ask bounce:
\[ S_{\text{Roll}, t} = 2\sqrt{\max\left(0,\, -\text{Cov}_t(\Delta p_t, \Delta p_{t-1})\right)} \]
  • Corwin & Schultz (2012) High-Low Spread: Exploits the fact that the 2-bar High-Low log range reflects twice the variance of a 1-bar range but only once the bid-ask spread:
\[ \beta_t = \left[\ln\frac{H_t}{L_t}\right]^2 + \left[\ln\frac{H_{t-1}}{L_{t-1}}\right]^2, \qquad \gamma_t = \left[\ln\frac{\max(H_t, H_{t-1})}{\min(L_t, L_{t-1})}\right]^2 \] \[ \alpha_t = \frac{\sqrt{2\beta_t} - \sqrt{\beta_t}}{3 - 2\sqrt{2}} - \sqrt{\frac{\gamma_t}{3 - 2\sqrt{2}}}, \qquad S_{\text{CS}, t} = \max\left(0,\, \frac{2(e^{\alpha_t} - 1)}{1 + e^{\alpha_t}}\right) \]

docs.title: kyle_lambda(close, volume, period=20, scale=1e6)
docs.text:
Kyle (1985) Market Depth / Price-Impact Coefficient (\(\lambda\)): Estimates the rolling OLS regression slope of price returns \(r_t\) on signed dollar order flow \(\text{SignedDV}_t = \text{sign}(r_t) \cdot P_t V_t\):

\[ \hat{\lambda}_t = \frac{\text{Cov}_t(r, \text{SignedDV})}{\text{Var}_t(\text{SignedDV})} \times \text{scale} \]

docs.title: 3. Index Futures Basis & Open Interest Regimes
futures_basis(futures_close, spot_close, days_to_expiry=None, period=20, annualization=365.0)

docs.title: hurst_exponent(close, period=50)
docs.text:
Rescaled Range (\(R/S\)) Hurst Exponent: For log returns \(r_1, \dots, r_n\) in a trailing window of length \(n\), let \(Z_k = \sum_{i=1}^k (r_i - \bar{r})\) be the cumulative mean-adjusted series:

\[ \frac{R_n}{S_n} = \frac{\max_{1 \le k \le n} Z_k - \min_{1 \le k \le n} Z_k}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n (r_i - \bar{r})^2}}, \qquad H_t = \frac{\ln(R_n / S_n)}{\ln(n)} \in [0, 1] \]
  • \(H_t > 0.5\): Persistent trending regime (momentum strategies favored).
  • \(H_t < 0.5\): Anti-persistent / mean-reverting regime (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck / Bollinger reversal favored).
  • \(H_t \approx 0.5\): Geometric Brownian Motion random walk.

docs.title: fractal_dimension(high, low, period=20) & entropy(close, period=20, bins=5)
docs.text:
• Ehlers' Fractal Dimension (\(D \in [1, 2]\)): Compares theHigh-Low range of the two half-windows (\(N_1, N_2\)) against the full window (\(N_3\)): \(D = \frac{\ln(N_1 + N_2) - \ln(N_3)}{\ln 2}\). Values near \(1.0\) indicate smooth straight-line trends; values near \(2.0\) indicate space-filling choppy noise.
  • Normalized Shannon Information Entropy (\(H \in [0, 1]\)): Partitions rolling returns into \(B\) empirical histogram bins with probabilities \(p_b\):
\[ H_t = -\frac{1}{\ln B} \sum_{b=1}^B p_b \ln(p_b) \]

docs.title: triple_barrier_labels(close, volatility=None, horizon=10, pt_mult=2.0, sl_mult=2.0, min_ret=0.0, vol_period=20, side=None)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation (López de Prado, 2018, Chapter 3): At each bar \(t\) with local volatility \(\sigma_t\) (defaulting to the \(20\)-bar rolling standard deviation of returns when volatility=None) and optional primary model directional prediction \(s_t = \text{sign}(\text{side}_t) \in \{-1, +1\}\):

\[ r_{t, t+k}^{\text{raw}} = \frac{P_{t+k} - P_t}{P_t}, \qquad r_{t, t+k}^{\text{dir}} = s_t \cdot r_{t, t+k}^{\text{raw}} \quad (k = 1, \dots, H) \]

The horizontal Profit-Taking (\(U_t\)) and Stop-Loss (\(L_t\)) thresholds are:

\[ U_t = \max\left(m_{\text{PT}} \cdot \sigma_t,\, r_{\min}\right), \qquad L_t = \max\left(m_{\text{SL}} \cdot \sigma_t,\, r_{\min}\right) \]

Let \(\tau_{\text{PT}} = \min\{k \le H : r_{t, t+k}^{\text{dir}} \ge U_t\}\) and \(\tau_{\text{SL}} = \min\{k \le H : r_{t, t+k}^{\text{dir}} \le -L_t\}\) (with \(\min \emptyset = H + 1\)).

Output pl.Struct Schema (alias="triple_barrier", prefix="tb_" when unnest=True): - label (Float64): \(+1.0\) if upper price barrier touched first, \(-1.0\) if lower price barrier touched first, or \(0.0\) if vertical expiration barrier \(H\) reached first. - touch_bars (Int64): First-passage time \(\tau^* = \min(\tau_{\text{PT}}, \tau_{\text{SL}}, H) \in \{1, \dots, H\}\). - realized_return (Float64): Raw price return \(r_{t, t+\tau^*}^{\text{raw}}\) at the touched barrier. - meta_label (Float64): Binary \(\{0.0, 1.0\}\) equal to \(1.0\) if and only if the trade in direction \(s_t\) hit its Profit-Taking barrier (\(\tau_{\text{PT}} < \tau_{\text{SL}}\) and \(\tau_{\text{PT}} \le H\)).

df = df.anta.triple_barrier_labels(
    close="close",
    horizon=12,
    pt_mult=2.0,
    sl_mult=1.5,
    side="primary_signal",
    unnest=True,
    group_by="symbol",
)

docs.title: trend_scanning_labels(close, min_window=5, max_window=20, step=1)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation (López de Prado, 2020): Fits forward OLS regressions \(P_{t+i} = \hat{\beta}_0(L) + \hat{\beta}_1(L)\,i + \epsilon_i\) across all candidate horizons \(L \in \{W_{\min}, \dots, W_{\max}\}\):

\[ t_{\hat{\beta}_1}(L) = \frac{\hat{\beta}_1(L)}{\sqrt{\frac{\text{SSR}(L) / (L - 2)}{\sum_{i=0}^{L-1}(i - \bar{i})^2}}}, \qquad L^*_t = \arg\max_{L} \left|t_{\hat{\beta}_1}(L)\right| \]

Output pl.Struct Schema (alias="trend_scan", prefix="ts_label_" when unnest=True): - label (Float64): Trend regime direction \(\text{sign}\left(t_{\hat{\beta}_1}(L^*_t)\right) \in \{-1.0, 0.0, +1.0\}\). - t_value (Float64): Signed optimal OLS \(t\)-statistic \(t_{\hat{\beta}_1}(L^*_t)\) (usable as sample weights in ML training). - optimal_window (Int64): Optimal lookahead window length \(L^*_t\). - ret (Float64): Forward return \((P_{t + L^*_t - 1} / P_t) - 1\).

docs.title: information_coefficient(df, factor_col, return_col, group_by=None, method="spearman")
docs.text:
Computes the cross-sectional Rank IC (method="spearman", default) or Pearson IC (method="pearson") time series:

\[ \text{RankIC}_t = \text{Corr}\left(\text{rank}(F_{i, t}),\, \text{rank}(R_{i, t \to t+h})\right) \]

docs.title: ic_summary(df, factor_col, return_col, group_by=None, method="spearman", nw_lags=None)
docs.text:
Computes IC summary metrics including Newey-West (1987) HAC autocorrelation-consistent \(t\)-statistics:

\[ \hat{\Omega}_{\text{NW}} = \hat{\gamma}_0 + 2 \sum_{j=1}^{L} \left(1 - \frac{j}{L + 1}\right) \hat{\gamma}_j, \qquad t_{\text{NW}} = \frac{\overline{\text{IC}}}{\sqrt{\hat{\Omega}_{\text{NW}} / T}} \]

When nw_lags=None, automatically selects the Newey-West (1994) plug-in bandwidth \(L = \max\left(1, \lfloor 4(T/100)^{2/9}\rfloor\right)\).

Student \(t\)-statistic \(\overline{\text{IC}} / (\hat{\sigma}_{\text{IC}} / \sqrt{T})\) \(\vert t\vert \ge 2.0\) (\(h = 1\) only) nw_t_stat Newey-West HAC \(t\)-statistic \(\overline{\text{IC}} / \sqrt{\hat{\Omega}_{\text{NW}} / T}\) \(\vert t_{\text{NW}}\vert \ge 2.0\) (robust to overlapping \(h > 1\)) hit_rate Fraction of periods with \(\text{IC}_t > 0\) \(\ge 55\%\) n_periods Total valid cross-sectional timestamps \(T\) —

docs.title: 4. Execution-Realistic Vectorized Backtesting & MAE/MFE Trade Ledger (polars_anta.backtest)
vectorized_backtest(df, ...) / df.anta.backtest(...)
docs.text: Executes a single-asset or multi-asset vectorized backtest with full execution realism: - Look-Ahead Prevention (signal_lag=1): Shifts target weights by 1 bar before multiplying by bar returns. - Execution Price Benchmarks (execution_price): - "close" (default): Close-to-Close bar returns. - "open": Next-Open to Open execution returns. - "twap": OHLC average \((O_t + H_t + L_t + C_t)/4\) execution returns. - "vwap": Typical price \((H_t + L_t + C_t)/3\) execution returns. - Intraday Session Flattening (flat_mask): Boolean expression forcing position = 0.0 on matching bars (e.g., closing intraday VN30F1M positions prior to the 14:30 ATC auction). - Dynamic Volatility Targeting (vol_target, vol_lookback=20, max_leverage=2.0): Scales position size by \(\min\left(L_{\max},\, \frac{\sigma_{\text{target}}}{\hat{\sigma}_{t-1}\sqrt{N_{\text{ann}}}}\right)\). - No-Trade Turnover Buffer (no_trade_buffer=0.0): Suppresses minor position adjustments where \(|w_t^{\text{target}} - w_{t-1}| \le \delta_{\text{buf}}\) unless exiting to 0.0.

docs.title: Statistical Inference, Multiple Testing & Factor Falsification (polars_anta.inference)
docs.text:
Modern quantitative research faces a severe multiple-testing and replication crisis. When a researcher screens \(K = 200\) technical indicators or alpha factors at a conventional \(\alpha = 5\%\) significance threshold (\(|t| > 1.96\)), roughly \(0.05 \times 200 = 10\) pure-noise signals will appear "statistically significant" by chance alone—even more when returns and Information Coefficients exhibit serial correlation (Harvey, Liu & Zhu, 2016; Jensen, Kelly & Pedersen, 2023).

polars_anta.inference provides a zero-SciPy, pure Polars + NumPy econometric falsification engine designed to separate genuine alpha from data-mining artifacts across time-series strategies and cross-sectional factor panels.

docs.title: End-to-End Falsification Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["Panel DataFrame / LazyFrame<br/>K Candidate Factors"] --> B["1. Joint IC Matrix<br/>ic_matrix() • Spearman / Pearson"]
    B --> C["2. HAC & Stationary Bootstrap<br/>Newey–West LRV • Politis–Romano (1994)"]
    C --> D["3. Multiple Testing Sieve<br/>BH/BY FDR • Romano–Wolf Stepdown<br/>Hansen SPA • CSCV PBO"]
    D --> E["4. Shrinkage & Stability<br/>Empirical Bayes (Efron–Morris)<br/>OLS-CUSUM • Breakeven Cost"]
    E --> F["FalsificationResult<br/>robust • fdr_only • decaying • noise"]

docs.title: How to Read a FalsificationResult
docs.text: Calling pa.falsify_factors(...) or df.anta.falsify_factors(...) executes a 7-stage statistical sieve and returns a FalsificationResult dataclass with .table (pl.DataFrame), .summary (dict), .ic_series (pl.DataFrame), and .report() (str).

docs.title: Verdict Classification Rules (Priority: decaying > robust > fdr_only > noise)
docs.text:
1. 'robust': Survives family-wise error rate control across all \(K\) tested factors (p_rw <= fwer_alpha, default \(\alpha = 0.05\)) and shows no statistically significant second-half attenuation.
  2. 'fdr_only': Fails strict FWER control (p_rw > fwer_alpha) but passes Benjamini–Hochberg False Discovery Rate control (q_bh <= fdr_q, default \(q = 0.10\)) without structural decay. Suitable for diversified multi-factor ensembles where a controlled proportion of false positives is acceptable.
  3. 'decaying': Statistically significant over the full sample (p_rw <= fwer_alpha or q_bh <= fdr_q), but rejects structural stability (p_cusum <= 0.05) with smaller magnitude in the second half of the sample (\(|\overline{\text{IC}}_{\text{second half}}| < |\overline{\text{IC}}_{\text{first half}}|\)). Signals alpha crowding or regime decay.
  4. 'noise': Cannot be distinguished from a zero-IC random series once multiple testing is accounted for (p_rw > fwer_alpha and q_bh > fdr_q).

docs.title: stationary_bootstrap_indices
docs.text:
Generates Politis & Romano (1994) Stationary Bootstrap index matrices of shape (n_boot, n_obs) with circular wrap-around and geometrically distributed block lengths (expected length \(L = \text{mean\_block}\), Continuation probability \(1 - 1/L\)):

\[ I_{b,0} \sim \text{Uniform}\{0, \dots, T - 1\}, \qquad I_{b,t} = \begin{cases} (I_{b,t-1} + 1) \bmod T & \text{with probability } 1 - \frac{1}{L} \\ U_{b,t} \sim \text{Uniform}\{0, \dots, T - 1\} & \text{with probability } \frac{1}{L} \end{cases} \]
  • Parameters: n_obs: int, n_boot: int = 1000, mean_block: float | None = None (defaults to \(\max(1, T^{1/3})\)), seed: int | None = None.
  • Citation: Politis & Romano (1994).
import polars_anta as pa

idx = pa.stationary_bootstrap_indices(n_obs=500, n_boot=1000, mean_block=10.0, seed=42)
assert idx.shape == (1000, 500)

docs.title: bootstrap_test
docs.text:
Performs a one-sample Stationary Bootstrap hypothesis test and percentile confidence interval for the sample mean or annualized Sharpe ratio against \(H_0: \theta = \text{null\_value}\):

\[ \hat{p} = \frac{1 + \sum_{b=1}^{B} \mathbb{I}\left(\tilde{\theta}^{\ast}_b \succeq \hat{\theta}\right)}{B + 1}, \qquad \tilde{\theta}^{\ast}_b = \theta^{\ast}_b - \hat{\theta} + \theta_0 \]

Vectorized via np.bincount weight matrices W @ X / T for the mean and sufficient moments \((\sum X, \sum X^2)\) for the Sharpe ratio without materializing 3-D bootstrap arrays.

  • Parameters: series, statistic: Literal["mean", "sharpe"] = "mean", null_value: float = 0.0, alternative: Literal["two-sided", "greater", "less"] = "two-sided", n_boot: int = 2000, mean_block: float | None = None, ci_level: float = 0.95, annualization: float = 252.0, seed: int | None = None.
  • Citation: Politis & Romano (1994).
import numpy as np
import polars_anta as pa

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
returns = rng.normal(loc=0.0008, scale=0.01, size=1000)
res = pa.bootstrap_test(returns, statistic="sharpe", annualization=252.0, n_boot=1000, seed=42)

docs.title: adjust_pvalues
docs.text:
Adjusts a vector of raw \(p\)-values for multiple hypothesis testing across \(m\) non-NaN hypotheses ordered as \(p_{(1)} \le p_{(2)} \le \dots \le p_{(m)}\):

  • Bonferroni ("bonferroni"): \(\tilde{p}_i = \min(1, m \cdot p_i)\)
  • Holm ("holm", 1979 step-down FWER): \(\tilde{p}_{(i)} = \min\left(1, \max_{j \le i} (m - j + 1) p_{(j)}\right)\)
  • Benjamini–Hochberg ("bh", 1995 step-up FDR): \(\tilde{p}_{(i)} = \min\left(1, \min_{j \ge i} \frac{m}{j} p_{(j)}\right)\)

  • Benjamini–Yekutieli ("by", 2001 arbitrary-dependence FDR): \(\tilde{p}_{(i)} = \min\left(1, c(m) \min_{j \ge i} \frac{m}{j} p_{(j)}\right)\) where \(c(m) = \sum_{k=1}^{m} \frac{1}{k}\)

  • Parameters: p_values, method: Literal["bonferroni", "holm", "bh", "by"] = "bh".

  • Citations: Holm (1979); Benjamini & Hochberg (1995); Benjamini & Yekutieli (2001).
import polars_anta as pa

raw_p = [0.005, 0.01, 0.03, 0.04, 0.25]
q_bh = pa.adjust_pvalues(raw_p, method="bh")
p_holm = pa.adjust_pvalues(raw_p, method="holm")

docs.title: romano_wolf
docs.text:
Implements the Romano & Wolf (2005, 2016) studentized stepdown \(\max\)-\(t\) multiple testing procedure using a shared Stationary Bootstrap index draw across all \(K\) strategies/factors to preserve cross-sectional dependence:

\[ t_k = \frac{\sqrt{T}\,\bar{X}_k}{\hat{\omega}_k}, \qquad t^{\ast}_{b,k} = \frac{\sqrt{T}\left(\bar{X}^{\ast}_{b,k} - \bar{X}_k\right)}{\hat{\omega}_k}, \qquad \hat{\omega}_k = \sqrt{T}\,\text{sd}_b\!\left(\bar{X}^{\ast}_{b,k}\right) \]

Ordering hypotheses as \(t_{(1)} \ge t_{(2)} \ge \dots \ge t_{(K)}\), stepdown adjusted \(p\)-values are computed in a single pass via backward cumulative maxima \(M^{\ast}_{b,j} = \max_{l \ge j} t^{\ast}_{b,(l)}\):

\[ \hat{p}^{\text{step}}_{(j)} = \frac{1 + \sum_{b=1}^{B} \mathbb{I}\left(M^{\ast}_{b,j} \ge t_{(j)}\right)}{B + 1}, \qquad \hat{p}^{\text{RW}}_{(j)} = \max_{i \le j} \hat{p}^{\text{step}}_{(i)} \]
  • Parameters: data, exclude: Sequence[str] = (), n_boot: int = 2000, mean_block: float | None = None, alternative: Literal["two-sided", "greater"] = "two-sided", seed: int | None = None.
  • Citations: Romano & Wolf (2005, 2016).
import numpy as np
import polars_anta as pa

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
mat = rng.standard_normal((500, 20))
mat[:, 0] += 0.18
rw_table = pa.romano_wolf(mat, n_boot=500, seed=7)

docs.title: spa_test
docs.text:
Tests the composite null hypothesis \(H_0: \max_{1 \le k \le K} \mathbb{E}[d_{k,t}] \le 0\) that no candidate strategy outperforms a benchmark, using Hansen's (2005) studentized Superior Predictive Ability statistic and White's (2000) Reality Check recentering bounds:

\[ T_{\text{SPA}} = \max\left(0, \max_{1 \le k \le K} \frac{\sqrt{T}\,\bar{d}_k}{\hat{\omega}_k}\right) \]

with three null recentering estimators \(g_k^{(l)} = \max(\bar{d}_k, 0)\), \(g_k^{(c)} = \bar{d}_k \cdot \mathbb{I}\!\left(\sqrt{T}\bar{d}_k/\hat{\omega}_k \ge -\sqrt{2\ln\ln T}\right)\), and \(g_k^{(u)} = \bar{d}_k\), guaranteeing \(p_{\text{lower}} \le p_{\text{consistent}} \le p_{\text{upper}}\).

  • Parameters: data, benchmark = None, exclude: Sequence[str] = (), n_boot: int = 2000, mean_block: float | None = None, seed: int | None = None.
  • Citations: White (2000); Hansen (2005).
import numpy as np
import polars_anta as pa

rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
excess_returns = rng.standard_normal((600, 30)) * 0.01
spa = pa.spa_test(excess_returns, benchmark=0.0, n_boot=500, seed=11)

docs.title: pbo_cscv
docs.text:
Estimates the Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO) via Combinatorially Symmetric Cross-Validation (Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado & Zhu, 2017). Splits a \((T, N)\) strategy return matrix into \(S\) equal sub-periods (\(S\) even) and evaluates \(\binom{S}{S/2}\) in-sample / out-of-sample partitions using pre-aggregated block sufficient moments (sum_s, sumsq_s):

\[ \bar{\omega}_c = \frac{\text{rank}_{\text{OOS}}(n^{\ast}_c)}{N + 1}, \qquad \lambda_c = \ln\left(\frac{\bar{\omega}_c}{1 - \bar{\omega}_c}\right), \qquad \text{PBO} = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{C}|} \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} \mathbb{I}(\lambda_c \le 0) \]
  • Parameters: data, exclude: Sequence[str] = (), n_splits: int = 16, max_combinations: int = 20_000, seed: int | None = None.
  • Citation: Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado & Zhu (2017).
import numpy as np
import polars_anta as pa

rng = np.random.default_rng(21)
strategy_matrix = rng.standard_normal((800, 12))
pbo_res = pa.pbo_cscv(strategy_matrix, n_splits=8)

docs.title: empirical_bayes_shrinkage
docs.text:
Applies Efron–Morris (1975) and Jensen, Kelly & Pedersen (2023) Empirical-Bayes hierarchical normal shrinkage across \(K\) noisy factor estimates \(\hat{\theta}_i\) with standard errors \(s_i\):

\[ \hat{\tau}^2 = \max\left(0,\; \frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{K} (\hat{\theta}_i - \mu_0)^2 - \frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{K} s_i^2\right), \qquad B_i = \frac{s_i^2}{s_i^2 + \hat{\tau}^2}, \qquad \hat{\theta}^{\text{EB}}_i = (1 - B_i)\hat{\theta}_i + B_i \mu_0 \]
  • Parameters: estimates, std_errors, names = None, prior: Literal["zero", "grand_mean"] = "zero", groups = None.
  • Citations: Efron & Morris (1975); Jensen, Kelly & Pedersen (2023).
import polars_anta as pa

eb_df = pa.empirical_bayes_shrinkage(
    estimates=[0.045, 0.012, -0.004, 0.038],
    std_errors=[0.010, 0.015, 0.014, 0.011],
    names=["mom_20", "rsi_14", "noise_1", "value_ebitda"],
)

docs.title: oos_r2, clark_west_test & diebold_mariano_test
docs.text:
Out-of-sample forecast evaluation against a historical benchmark or competing model:

  • oos_r2 (Campbell & Thompson, 2008): $\(R^2_{\text{OOS}} = 1 - \frac{\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} (y_t - \hat{y}_t)^2}{\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} (y_t - \bar{y}_t)^2}\)$
  • clark_west_test (Clark & West, 2007 nested model MSPE-adjusted test): $\(f_t = (y_t - \hat{y}_{0,t})^2 - \left[(y_t - \hat{y}_{1,t})^2 - (\hat{y}_{0,t} - \hat{y}_{1,t})^2\right], \qquad t_{\text{CW}} = \frac{\bar{f}}{\widehat{\text{se}}_{\text{NW}}(\bar{f})} \quad (\text{one-sided } H_1: \mathbb{E}[f_t] > 0)\)$
  • diebold_mariano_test (Diebold & Mariano, 1995 equal predictive accuracy test): $\(d_t = L(e_{1,t}) - L(e_{2,t}), \qquad \text{DM} = \frac{\bar{d}}{\widehat{\text{se}}_{\text{NW}}(\bar{d})}\)$
import numpy as np
import polars_anta as pa

rng = np.random.default_rng(99)
y_true = rng.normal(0.001, 0.02, size=300)
y_bench = np.zeros_like(y_true)
y_model = 0.25 * y_true + rng.normal(0.0, 0.005, size=300)

r2_val = pa.oos_r2(y_true, y_model, benchmark=y_bench)
cw_res = pa.clark_west_test(y_true, y_model, y_bench)
dm_res = pa.diebold_mariano_test(y_true, y_model, y_bench, loss="squared")

docs.title: cusum_mean_test
docs.text:
Tests structural stability of a factor IC or strategy return series via the Ploberger & Krämer (1992) HAC-standardized OLS-CUSUM Brownian bridge supremum statistic:

\[ W_T(k) = \frac{1}{\hat{\sigma}_{\text{NW}}\sqrt{T}} \sum_{t=1}^{k} \left(x_t - \bar{x}_T\right), \qquad S_T = \max_{1 \le k \le T} \left|W_T(k)\right|, \qquad p_{\text{CUSUM}} \approx 2 \sum_{j=1}^{100} (-1)^{j-1} \exp\!\left(-2 j^2 S_T^2\right) \]
  • Parameters: series, nw_lags: int | None = None.
  • Citation: Ploberger & Krämer (1992).
import numpy as np
import polars_anta as pa

ic_series = np.concatenate([np.full(150, 0.04), np.full(150, -0.01)])
cusum = pa.cusum_mean_test(ic_series)

docs.title: breakeven_cost & breakeven_cost_from_backtest
docs.text:
Computes the exact per-unit-turnover transaction cost rate \(c^{\ast}\) (reported in both decimal and basis points) at which a strategy's mean net return or net Sharpe ratio is driven to zero:

\[ c^{\ast} = \frac{\sum_{t=1}^{T} r^{\text{gross}}_t}{\sum_{t=1}^{T} \tau_t}, \qquad \text{where } \sum_{t=1}^{T} \left(r^{\text{gross}}_t - c^{\ast} \tau_t\right) = 0 \] 
import polars_anta as pa

cost_info = pa.breakeven_cost(gross_returns=[0.002, 0.001, -0.0005], turnover=[0.5, 0.25, 0.25])

docs.title: FalsificationResult & falsify_factors
docs.text:
Runs the complete 7-stage statistical falsification funnel on a multi-asset panel DataFrame or LazyFrame. Exposed both at top level (pa.falsify_factors) and on .anta / .ta frame namespaces (df.anta.falsify_factors):

import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import polars_anta as pa

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
n_dates, n_assets = 80, 25
dates = np.repeat(np.arange(n_dates), n_assets)
fwd = rng.normal(0.0, 0.02, size=n_dates * n_assets)

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "date": dates,
        "fwd_ret": fwd,
        "true_alpha": 0.35 * fwd + rng.normal(0.0, 0.02, size=n_dates * n_assets),
        "noise_alpha": rng.normal(0.0, 1.0, size=n_dates * n_assets),
    }
)

result = df.anta.falsify_factors(
    factor_cols=["true_alpha", "noise_alpha"],
    return_col="fwd_ret",
    group_by="date",
    horizon=1,
    n_boot=299,
    seed=42,
)
print(result.report())
