docs.title: Momentum Oscillators & Cycle Transforms (polars_anta.momentum)
docs.text: The polars_anta.momentum module provides 22 velocity oscillators, double-smoothed momentum filters, Gaussian Fisher transforms, and volatility-squeeze cycle detectors.

docs.title: rsi(close, period=14) & cmo(close, period=14)
docs.text:
Let \(\Delta C_t = C_t - C_{t-1}\), \(U_t = \max(\Delta C_t, 0)\), and \(D_t = \max(-\Delta C_t, 0)\). - Wilder's Relative Strength Index (rsi): Uses Wilder's recursive smoothing \(\bar{U}_t = \text{RMA}_n(U_t)\) and \(\bar{D}_t = \text{RMA}_n(D_t)\):

\[ \text{RS}_t = \frac{\bar{U}_t}{\bar{D}_t}, \qquad \text{RSI}_t = 100 - \frac{100}{1 + \text{RS}_t} = 100 \frac{\bar{U}_t}{\bar{U}_t + \bar{D}_t} \in [0, 100] \]
  • Chande Momentum Oscillator (cmo): Uses unsmoothed rolling sums over \(n\) bars and scales symmetrically into \([-100, +100]\):
\[ \text{CMO}_t = 100 \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} U_{t-i} - \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} D_{t-i}}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} U_{t-i} + \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} D_{t-i}} \in [-100, +100] \]

docs.title: stochastic(high, low, close, k_period=14, d_period=3, smooth_k=1), stoch_rsi(...), & williams_r(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text:
Let \(H_t^{(n)} = \max_{0 \le i < n} H_{t-i}\) and \(L_t^{(n)} = \min_{0 \le i < n} L_{t-i}\):

\[ \%K_t^{\text{raw}} = 100 \frac{C_t - L_t^{(n)}}{H_t^{(n)} - L_t^{(n)}} \in [0, 100], \qquad \%R_t = -100 \frac{H_t^{(n)} - C_t}{H_t^{(n)} - L_t^{(n)}} = \%K_t^{\text{raw}} - 100 \in [-100, 0] \]
  • stochastic returns Struct(k, d) where \(k = \text{SMA}_{n_k}(\%K^{\text{raw}})\) and \(d = \text{SMA}_{n_d}(k)\) (using smoothing parameters smooth_k and d_period).
  • stoch_rsi applies the Stochastic normalization directly to the \(\text{RSI}_t\) series, returning Struct(k, d).

docs.title: macd(close, fast_period=12, slow_period=26, signal_period=9) & ppo(close, fast_period=12, slow_period=26, signal_period=9)
docs.text:
• MACD (Struct(macd, signal, histogram)):
\[ \text{MACD}_t = \text{EMA}_{12}(C_t) - \text{EMA}_{26}(C_t), \quad \text{Signal}_t = \text{EMA}_9(\text{MACD}_t), \quad \text{Hist}_t = \text{MACD}_t - \text{Signal}_t \]
  • Percentage Price Oscillator (ppo, Struct(ppo, signal, histogram)): Normalizes MACD by \(\text{EMA}_{26}(C_t)\) so momentum magnitudes can be compared across assets at different price levels:
\[ \text{PPO}_t = \frac{\text{EMA}_{12}(C_t) - \text{EMA}_{26}(C_t)}{\text{EMA}_{26}(C_t)} \times 100 \]

docs.title: tsi(close, long_period=25, short_period=13)
docs.text:
William Blau's True Strength Index: Applies a cascaded double-EMA filter to both raw price change \(\Delta C_t\) and absolute price change \(|\Delta C_t|\):

\[ \text{TSI}_t = 100 \cdot \frac{\text{EMA}_{13}\!\left(\text{EMA}_{25}(\Delta C_t)\right)}{\text{EMA}_{13}\!\left(\text{EMA}_{25}(|\Delta C_t|)\right)} \in [-100, +100] \]

Because the denominator normalizes by double-smoothed volatility, tsi acts as a high-signal-to-noise continuous Sharpe-like momentum oscillator.

docs.title: trix(close, period=15, signal_period=9)
docs.text:
Jack Hutson's Triple Exponential Average (Struct(trix, signal)): Triple-smooths close with the same EMA span, then takes the one-bar percentage rate of change. The signal line is an EMA of that oscillator:

\[ \text{EMA}_{1} = \text{EMA}_n(C), \quad \text{EMA}_{2} = \text{EMA}_n(\text{EMA}_{1}), \quad \text{EMA}_{3} = \text{EMA}_n(\text{EMA}_{2}) \] \[ \text{TRIX}_t = 100 \times \frac{\text{EMA}_{3,t} - \text{EMA}_{3,t-1}}{\text{EMA}_{3,t-1}}, \qquad \text{Signal}_t = \text{EMA}_m(\text{TRIX}_t) \]

docs.title: fisher_transform(high, low, period=10)
docs.text:
John Ehlers' Fisher Transform (Struct(fisher, trigger)): Empirical financial price series have approximately uniform or leptokurtic distributions within a rolling channel, meaning extreme readings do not cluster cleanly at turning points. Ehlers first normalizes midpoint price \(M_t = (H_t + L_t)/2\) into \((-1, +1)\) (smoothed via \(X_t\) and clipped to \((-0.999, +0.999)\)) and applies the inverse hyperbolic tangent (Fisher \(z\)-transformation):

\[ F_t = \frac{1}{2} \ln\!\left(\frac{1 + X_t}{1 - X_t}\right) + \frac{1}{2} F_{t-1} = \operatorname{artanh}(X_t) + \frac{1}{2} F_{t-1} \]

This maps bounded price position into an approximately Gaussian normal distribution with sharp, unambiguous probability spikes at cycle reversals.

docs.title: squeeze_momentum(high, low, close, bb_period=20, bb_mult=2.0, kc_period=20, kc_mult=1.5)
docs.text: John Carter's Volatility Squeeze & Linear Regression Momentum (Struct(momentum, squeeze_on, squeeze_off, no_squeeze)): 1. Volatility Compression Detection: - squeeze_on (Boolean): \(\text{BB}_{\text{upper}, t} < \text{KC}_{\text{upper}, t} \;\land\; \text{BB}_{\text{lower}, t} > \text{KC}_{\text{lower}, t}\) (Bollinger Bands contract completely inside Keltner Channels during low-volatility consolidation). - squeeze_off (Boolean): Bollinger Bands expand outside Keltner Channels, signaling an explosive volatility breakout. 2. Directional Momentum Histogram: Computes the deviation of \(C_t\) from the average of the Donchian midline and SMA, smoothed via closed-form OLS linear regression forecast (linear_regression_forecast).

docs.title: stc(close, fast_period=23, slow_period=50, cycle_period=10, smooth_period=3)
docs.text: Doug Schaff's Trend Cycle Oscillator: Cascades two successive Stochastic-EMA cycle normalizations over the MACD line (\(\text{MACD}_{23, 50}\)), detecting cyclical turns significantly faster than standard MACD while remaining bounded in \([0, 100]\).

docs.title: Quantitative Statistics, CAPM & Regression Transforms (polars_anta.stats)
docs.text: The polars_anta.stats module provides 15 vectorized statistical, econometric, and stationarity primitives engineered for factor standardization, systematic risk decomposition, rolling Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, and memory-preserving fractional differentiation.

docs.title: zscore(close, period=20)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation:

\[ Z_t = \frac{x_t - \hat{\mu}_t}{\hat{\sigma}_t}, \qquad \hat{\mu}_t = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_{t-i}, \qquad \hat{\sigma}_t = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n - 1}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_{t-i} - \hat{\mu}_t)^2} \]
  • Quantitative Interpretation: Measures how many rolling standard deviations the current observation lies away from its trailing mean. Widely used in statistical arbitrage (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck mean-reversion triggers when \(|Z_t| > 2.0\)) and time-series feature normalization.
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Pure native Rust rolling_mean(period) and rolling_std(period) with zero-division protection (0.0 when \(\hat{\sigma}_t = 0\)).

docs.title: percentile_rank(close, period=20)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation:

\[ \text{PctRank}_t = \frac{1}{n - 1} \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \left( \mathbb{I}_{\{x_{t-i} < x_t\}} + \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{I}_{\{x_{t-i} = x_t\}} \right) \in [0.0, 1.0] \]
  • Quantitative Interpretation: Non-parametric, outlier-resistant alternative to zscore. Because financial returns exhibit heavy tails where a single volatility shock can distort \(\hat{\sigma}_t\) for \(n\) subsequent bars, percentile_rank maps any fat-tailed distribution uniformly onto \([0, 1]\).
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Vectorized via zero-copy sliding_window_view pairwise comparison against the rightmost column windows[:, -1:].

docs.title: skewness(close, period=20) & kurtosis(close, period=20)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulations:

\[ \hat{\gamma}_{3, t} = \frac{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_{t-i} - \hat{\mu}_t)^3}{\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_{t-i} - \hat{\mu}_t)^2\right)^{3/2}}, \qquad \hat{\gamma}_{4, t} = \frac{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_{t-i} - \hat{\mu}_t)^4}{\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_{t-i} - \hat{\mu}_t)^2\right)^{2}} - 3 \]
  • Quantitative Interpretation:
  • Skewness (\(\hat{\gamma}_3\)): Quantifies distributional asymmetry. Negative return skewness (\(\hat{\gamma}_3 < 0\)) warns of "crash risk" (frequent small gains punctuated by sharp drawdowns, typical of short-volatility or carry strategies).
  • Excess Kurtosis (\(\hat{\gamma}_4\)): Quantifies tail thickness relative to a Gaussian distribution (\(\gamma_4^{\text{normal}} = 0\)). High excess kurtosis signals regime instability and elevated probability of \(3\sigma+\) tail events.
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Delegated directly to Polars' native streaming rolling_skew(period) and rolling_kurtosis(period) kernels in Rust.

docs.title: rolling_cov(x, y, period=20) & rolling_corr(x, y, period=20)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulations:

\[ \text{Cov}_t(X, Y) = \frac{1}{n - 1} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (x_{t-i} - \bar{x}_t)(y_{t-i} - \bar{y}_t), \qquad \rho_t(X, Y) = \frac{\text{Cov}_t(X, Y)}{\hat{\sigma}_{X, t}\,\hat{\sigma}_{Y, t}} \in [-1, 1] \]
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Computed via Polars' native pl.rolling_cov(x, y, window_size=period) and pl.rolling_corr(x, y, window_size=period) in Rust.

docs.title: rolling_beta(asset_returns, benchmark_returns, period=60) & rolling_alpha(asset_returns, benchmark_returns, rf=0.0, period=60)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulations (Sharpe-Lintner CAPM):

\[ \hat{\beta}_t = \frac{\text{Cov}_t(R_a, R_m)}{\text{Var}_t(R_m)}, \qquad \hat{\alpha}_t = (\bar{R}_{a, t} - r_f) - \hat{\beta}_t (\bar{R}_{m, t} - r_f) \]
  • Quantitative Interpretation:
  • rolling_beta measures time-varying systematic exposure of an asset or strategy \(R_a\) to the market benchmark \(R_m\) (e.g., VN30 Index). It is the foundational input for constructing Beta-Neutral long/short portfolios (\(w_i^{\text{hedged}} = w_i - \hat{\beta}_i w_m\)) and passing into orthogonalize.
  • rolling_alpha (Jensen's Alpha) isolates idiosyncratic return per period unexplained by systematic market drift.

docs.title: 3. Closed-Form Rolling OLS Linear Regression Suite
docs.text:
Fitting \(y_{t-n+1+i} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot i + \epsilon_i\) for \(i \in \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}\) via exact WMA–SMA algebraic reduction (see Architecture & Mathematical Derivations):

Function Signature Closed-Form Identity Quantitative Use Case linear_regression_slope(close, period=14) \(\hat{\beta}_1 = \frac{6}{n - 1}\left(\text{WMA}_n - \text{SMA}_n\right)\) Velocity of price change per bar (\(112.4\times\) faster than a pandas rolling().apply() baseline). linear_regression_intercept(close, period=14) \(\hat{\beta}_0 = 4\,\text{SMA}_n - 3\,\text{WMA}_n\) Fitted value at the start of the rolling window (\(i = 0\)). linear_regression_forecast(close, period=14) \(\hat{y}_t = \hat{\beta}_0 + \hat{\beta}_1(n - 1) = 3\,\text{WMA}_n - 2\,\text{SMA}_n\) Zero-lag OLS end-of-window fair value estimate. linear_regression_angle(close, period=14) \(\theta_t = \arctan(\hat{\beta}_1) \cdot \frac{180}{\pi}\) Trend trajectory angle in degrees \((-90^\circ, +90^\circ)\). linear_regression_r2(close, period=14) \(R^2_t = \text{clip}\left(\hat{\beta}_1^2 \cdot \frac{n(n + 1)}{12\,\text{Var}_s(y)},\, 0,\, 1\right)\) Rolling OLS goodness-of-fit (\(R^2 \in [0, 1]\)) measuring trend linearity vs. noise. linear_regression_stderr(close, period=14) \(s_{\hat{y}, t} = \sqrt{\frac{n - 1}{n - 2}\,\text{Var}_s(y)\,(1 - R^2_t)}\) Rolling OLS standard error of the estimate (\(\sqrt{\text{SSR}/(n-2)}\)) in price units. 
import polars as pl
import polars_anta as pa

df = df.with_columns(
    pl.col("close").anta.linear_regression_r2(period=14).alias("ols_r2_14"),
    pl.col("close").anta.linear_regression_stderr(period=14).alias("ols_se_14"),
)

docs.title: frac_diff(close, d=0.4, window=20)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation (Fixed-Window Fractional Differentiation — López de Prado, 2018):

\[ \tilde{X}_t^{(d, W)} = \sum_{k=0}^{W-1} \omega_k X_{t-k}, \qquad \omega_0 = 1, \qquad \omega_k = -\omega_{k-1} \frac{d - k + 1}{k} \quad (k = 1, \dots, W - 1) \]
  • Quantitative Theory:
  • When \(d = 0.0\), \(\omega_0 = 1\) and \(\omega_k = 0\) (\(\forall k \ge 1\)), returning the raw non-stationary price series \(X_t\).
  • When \(d = 1.0\), \(\omega_0 = 1, \omega_1 = -1\), and \(\omega_k = 0\) (\(\forall k \ge 2\)), returning the standard first difference \(X_t - X_{t-1}\) (which is stationary but erases trend memory).
  • For fractional orders \(d \in (0, 1)\) (typically \(d \in [0.3, 0.5]\)), all weights \(\omega_k\) (\(k \ge 1\)) are negative and decay slowly according to a power law \(\omega_k \sim \frac{-d}{\Gamma(1-d)} k^{-d-1}\). This transformation removes unit-root non-stationarity so tree/neural ML models do not overfit to secular price levels, while preserving long-memory cointegration and support/resistance structure.
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Precomputes the exact binomial weight vector w_rev = weights[::-1] once and executes a single BLAS matrix-vector product sliding_window_view(vals, window) @ w_rev inside map_batches, supporting multi-asset .over("symbol") partitioning.
import polars as pl
import polars_anta as pa

df = df.with_columns(
    pl.col("close").anta.frac_diff(d=0.4, window=20).over("symbol").alias("close_ffd_04")
)

docs.title: Trend Filters, Adaptive Moving Averages & Structural Pivots (polars_anta.trend)
docs.text: The polars_anta.trend module provides 28 low-lag moving averages, adaptive digital filters, directional regime classifiers, volatility trailing stops, and structural pivot levels.

docs.title: 1. Linear, Low-Lag & Gaussian Moving Averages
docs.text:
In digital signal processing (DSP), a moving average is a low-pass filter that attenuates high-frequency market noise at the cost of phase lag. polars-anta provides a full hierarchy of linear and zero-lag filters:

Function Signature Mathematical Definition Phase Lag & Filter Characteristics sma(close, period=10) \(\text{SMA}_t(n) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} C_{t-i}\) Equal weights; group delay of \(\frac{n - 1}{2}\) bars. ema(close, period=10) \(\text{EMA}_t(n) = \alpha C_t + (1 - \alpha)\text{EMA}_{t-1}(n), \quad \alpha = \frac{2}{n + 1}\) Infinite impulse response (IIR) filter; center-of-mass lag of \(\frac{n - 1}{2}\) bars with higher recent weight. wma(close, period=10) \(\text{WMA}_t(n) = \frac{2}{n(n + 1)} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (n - i) C_{t-i}\) Triangular weight profile; reduces group delay to \(\frac{n - 1}{3}\) bars. hma(close, period=10) \(\text{HMA}_t(n) = \text{WMA}_{\lfloor\sqrt{n}\rfloor}\!\left(2\,\text{WMA}_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}(C_t) - \text{WMA}_n(C_t)\right)\) Alan Hull's algebraic lag cancellation; eliminates first-order linear phase lag while maintaining smoothness. dema(close, period=10) \(\text{DEMA}_t = 2 E_1 - E_2\), where \(E_1 = \text{EMA}_n(C), E_2 = \text{EMA}_n(E_1)\) Patrick Mulloy's second-order error-correcting exponential filter. tema(close, period=10) \(\text{TEMA}_t = 3 E_1 - 3 E_2 + E_3\), where \(E_3 = \text{EMA}_n(E_2)\) Third-order error cancellation for steep trend tracking. zlema(close, period=10) \(\text{ZLEMA}_t = \text{EMA}_n\!\left(C_t + (C_t - C_{t - \lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor})\right)\) Pre-compensates input price by adding the momentum over the filter's half-window lag. t3(close, period=5, vfactor=0.7) \(\text{T3}_t = c_1 E_6 + c_2 E_5 + c_3 E_4 + c_4 E_3\) (\(6\)-stage cascaded EMA) Tim Tillson's generalized DEMA cascade; combines low phase lag with minimal overshoot. alma(close, period=9, offset=0.85, sigma=6.0) \(\text{ALMA}_t = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} w_i C_{t-n+1+i}}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} w_i}, \quad w_i = \exp\!\left(-\frac{(i - m)^2}{2 s^2}\right)\) Arnaud Legoux's shifted Gaussian bell-curve convolution (\(m = \text{offset}(n-1), s = n/\sigma\)).

docs.title: 2. Non-Linear Adaptive Moving Averages
docs.text: Unlike fixed-period filters, adaptive moving averages dynamically modulate their smoothing constant \(\alpha_t\) based on market efficiency or momentum:

docs.title: kama(close, period=10, fast_period=2, slow_period=30)
docs.text:
Perry Kaufman's Adaptive Moving Average: Computes the Efficiency Ratio (\(\text{ER}_t \in [0, 1]\)) — the ratio of net directional displacement to total path length:

\[ \text{ER}_t = \frac{|C_t - C_{t-n}|}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} |C_{t-i} - C_{t-i-1}|}, \qquad \text{SC}_t = \left[ \text{ER}_t (\alpha_{\text{fast}} - \alpha_{\text{slow}}) + \alpha_{\text{slow}} \right]^2 \] \[ \text{KAMA}_t = \text{KAMA}_{t-1} + \text{SC}_t (C_t - \text{KAMA}_{t-1}) \]

When price moves in a straight line (\(\text{ER}_t \to 1\)), \(\text{KAMA}_t\) tracks closely at fast_period; during sideways chop (\(\text{ER}_t \to 0\)), \(\text{SC}_t^2 \to \alpha_{\text{slow}}^2\), freezing the average flat to prevent whipsaws.

docs.title: vidya(close, period=14, hist_period=None) & mcginley_dynamic(close, period=14)
docs.text:
• Tushar Chande's VIDYA: Modulates \(\alpha_t = \alpha_0 \cdot |\text{CMO}_t| / 100\) using the absolute Chande Momentum Oscillator.
  • John McGinley's Dynamic Indicator: Adjusts smoothing inversely to the fourth power of price velocity:
\[ \text{MD}_t = \text{MD}_{t-1} + \frac{C_t - \text{MD}_{t-1}}{n \cdot (C_t / \text{MD}_{t-1})^4} \]

docs.title: 3. Directional Strength, Regime Classifiers & Trailing Stops
adx(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text:
J. Welles Wilder's Directional Movement System (pl.Struct: ("adx", "plus_di", "minus_di")):

\[ \text{+DM}_t = \max(H_t - H_{t-1}, 0)\,\mathbb{I}_{\{H_t - H_{t-1} > L_{t-1} - L_t\}}, \qquad \text{-DM}_t = \max(L_{t-1} - L_t, 0)\,\mathbb{I}_{\{L_{t-1} - L_t > H_t - H_{t-1}\}} \] \[ \text{+DI}_t = 100 \frac{\text{RMA}_n(\text{+DM}_t)}{\text{ATR}_t(n)}, \qquad \text{-DI}_t = 100 \frac{\text{RMA}_n(\text{-DM}_t)}{\text{ATR}_t(n)} \] \[ \text{DX}_t = 100 \frac{|\text{+DI}_t - \text{-DI}_t|}{\text{+DI}_t + \text{-DI}_t}, \qquad \text{ADX}_t = \text{RMA}_n(\text{DX}_t) \]

docs.title: chop(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text:
E.W. Dreiss's Choppiness Index (Fractal Consolidation Filter):

\[ \text{CHOP}_t(n) = 100 \cdot \frac{\log_{10}\!\left(\frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \text{TR}_{t-i}}{\max_{0 \le i < n} H_{t-i} - \min_{0 \le i < n} L_{t-i}}\right)}{\log_{10}(n)} \in [0, 100] \]
  • \(\text{CHOP}_t > 61.8\): Market is range-bound / consolidating (Fibonacci retracement threshold).
  • \(\text{CHOP}_t < 38.2\): Strong directional trend is underway.

docs.title: supertrend(high, low, close, period=10, multiplier=3.0) & psar(high, low, close=None, af_start=0.02, af_step=0.02, af_max=0.20)
docs.text:
• supertrend: Stateful ATR ratchet stop around \(\text{HL2}_t = (H_t + L_t)/2 \pm m \cdot \text{ATR}_t(n)\). Returns Struct(supertrend, direction) where direction is +1 (bullish) or -1 (bearish).
  • psar (Parabolic SAR): Wilder's accelerating stop-and-reverse parabola \(\text{SAR}_{t+1} = \text{SAR}_t + \text{AF}_t (\text{EP}_t - \text{SAR}_t)\) where the acceleration factor \(\text{AF}_t\) increments by af_step up to af_max whenever a new Extreme Point (\(\text{EP}_t\)) is reached.

docs.title: vortex, aroon, mass_index, ssl_channel, trend_intensity_index, center_of_gravity
docs.text: Function Signature Output Type / Struct Fields Mathematical Mechanism vortex(high, low, close, period=14) Struct(vi_plus, vi_minus) \(\text{VI}^\pm_t = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \vert H_{t-i} - L_{t-i-1}\vert }{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \text{TR}_{t-i}}\) (Botes & Siepman, 2010) aroon(high, low, period=14) Struct(aroon_up, aroon_down, oscillator) \(\text{AroonUp}_t = \frac{n - \tau_{\text{high}, n}}{n} \times 100\) (Tushar Chande, 1995) mass_index(high, low, ema_period=9, sum_period=25) Float64 \(\sum_{i=0}^{24} \frac{\text{EMA}_9(H - L)_{t-i}}{\text{EMA}_9(\text{EMA}_9(H - L))_{t-i}}\) (Donald Dorsey reversal bulge \(> 27\)) ssl_channel(high, low, close, period=10) Struct(ssl_down, ssl_up) State-flipped SMA(High) and SMA(Low) channel lines trend_intensity_index(close, sma_period=60, period=30) Float64 M.H. Pee's percentage of positive deviations above \(\text{SMA}_{60}\) \([0, 100]\) center_of_gravity(close, period=10) Float64 John Ehlers' zero-lag cycle oscillator \(-\frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(i + 1)C_{t-i}}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} C_{t-i}}\)

docs.title: 4. Cloud Overlays, Heikin-Ashi & Structural Pivot Points
docs.text: Function Signature Output pl.Struct Schema Formulation ichimoku(high, low, close, tenkan=9, kijun=26, senkou_b=52, displacement=26) Struct(tenkan_sen, kijun_sen, senkou_span_a, senkou_span_b, chikou_span) Donchian midpoints over \(9, 26, 52\) bars with forward/backward cloud displacement heikin_ashi(open, high, low, close) Struct(ha_open, ha_high, ha_low, ha_close) Loop-free synthetic candlesticks via exact \(\text{EMA}(\alpha=0.5)\) reduction pivot_points(high, low, close) Struct(pivot, r1, r2, r3, s1, s2, s3) Classical Floor Trader pivots around \(P = (H_{t-1} + L_{t-1} + C_{t-1})/3\) fibonacci_pivots(high, low, close) Struct(pivot, r1, r2, r3, s1, s2, s3) \(P \pm \{0.382, 0.618, 1.000\} \times (H_{t-1} - L_{t-1})\) camarilla_pivots(high, low, close) Struct(pivot, r1, r2, r3, r4, s1, s2, s3, s4) Nick Scott's intraday mean-reversion/breakout levels \(C_{t-1} \pm \frac{1.1}{2, 4, 6, 12}(H_{t-1} - L_{t-1})\) woodie_pivots(high, low, close) Struct(pivot, r1, r2, s1, s2) Close-weighted pivot \(P = (H_{t-1} + L_{t-1} + 2 C_{t-1})/4\)

docs.title: Volatility Estimators, ATR Stops & Price Channels (polars_anta.volatility)
docs.text: The polars_anta.volatility module provides 20 volatility estimators, range-based efficient variance models, and dynamic price channels used for position sizing, volatility targeting, breakout detection, and stop-loss placement.

docs.title: 1. High-Efficiency Range-Based Volatility Estimators
docs.text:
In continuous-time finance (\(d\ln P_t = \sigma\,dW_t\)), the standard Close-to-Close volatility estimator uses only two snapshots per bar (\(C_{t-1}\) and \(C_t\)), discarding all intraday path information (a stock that surges \(+5\%\) intraday and closes unchanged has zero close-to-close return).

polars-anta implements five classical annualized volatility estimators with increasing statistical asymptotic efficiency \(\text{Eff}(\hat{\sigma}^2) = \frac{\text{Var}(\hat{\sigma}_{\text{CC}}^2)}{\text{Var}(\hat{\sigma}^2)}\):

Estimator Function Signature Mathematical Formula (Annualized by \(\sqrt{A}\), default \(A = 252\)) Statistical Efficiency Close-to-Close historical_volatility(close, period=20, trading_periods=252) \(\hat{\sigma}_{\text{CC}, t} = \sqrt{A} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{1}{n - 1}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \left(r_{t-i} - \bar{r}_t\right)^2}, \quad r_t = \ln\frac{C_t}{C_{t-1}}\) \(1.0\times\) (Baseline) Parkinson (1980) parkinson_volatility(high, low, period=20, trading_periods=252) \(\hat{\sigma}_{\text{P}, t} = \sqrt{A} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{1}{4 n \ln 2} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \left(\ln\frac{H_{t-i}}{L_{t-i}}\right)^2}\) \(4.9\times\) Garman-Klass (1980) garman_klass_volatility(open, high, low, close, period=20, trading_periods=252) \(\hat{\sigma}_{\text{GK}, t} = \sqrt{A} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \left[\frac{1}{2}\left(\ln\frac{H_{t-i}}{L_{t-i}}\right)^2 - (2\ln 2 - 1)\left(\ln\frac{C_{t-i}}{O_{t-i}}\right)^2\right]}\) \(7.4\times\) Rogers-Satchell (1991) rogers_satchell_volatility(open, high, low, close, period=20, trading_periods=252) \(\hat{\sigma}_{\text{RS}, t} = \sqrt{A} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \left[\ln\frac{H_{t-i}}{C_{t-i}}\ln\frac{H_{t-i}}{O_{t-i}} + \ln\frac{L_{t-i}}{C_{t-i}}\ln\frac{L_{t-i}}{O_{t-i}}\right]}\) \(6.0\times\) (Drift-independent) Yang-Zhang (2000) yang_zhang_volatility(open, high, low, close, period=20, trading_periods=252) \(\hat{\sigma}_{\text{YZ}, t} = \sqrt{A} \cdot \sqrt{\hat{\sigma}_o^2 + k\,\hat{\sigma}_c^2 + (1 - k)\,\hat{\sigma}_{\text{RS}}^2}, \quad k = \frac{0.34}{1.34 + \frac{n + 1}{n - 1}}\) \(14.0\times\) (Drift & overnight jump robust) 
import polars as pl
import polars_anta as pa

df = df.with_columns(
    pa.rogers_satchell_volatility("open", "high", "low", "close", period=20).alias("rs_vol_20"),
    pa.yang_zhang_volatility("open", "high", "low", "close", period=20).alias("yz_vol_20"),
)

Quantitative Advantage of Garman-Klass

Because Garman-Klass achieves \(7.4\times\) higher statistical efficiency than Close-to-Close volatility, a 10-bar Garman-Klass estimator has lower estimation variance than a 70-bar Close-to-Close estimator, enabling much faster regime adaptation in Volatility Targeting (vol_target) and Triple-Barrier scaling without increasing estimation noise.

docs.title: 2. True Range, Wilder's ATR & Trailing Volatility Stops
true_range(high, low, close), atr(high, low, close, period=14), & natr(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulations (J. Welles Wilder Jr., 1978):

\[ \text{TR}_t = \max\left(H_t - L_t,\, |H_t - C_{t-1}|,\, |L_t - C_{t-1}|\right) \] \[ \text{ATR}_t(n) = \text{RMA}_n(\text{TR}_t) = \frac{(n - 1)\,\text{ATR}_{t-1} + \text{TR}_t}{n}, \qquad \text{NATR}_t(n) = \frac{\text{ATR}_t(n)}{C_t} \times 100 \]
  • Quantitative Interpretation: true_range accounts for overnight or inter-bar gaps (\(|H_t - C_{t-1}|\) and \(|L_t - C_{t-1}|\)). While atr is denominated in raw price points (ideal for sizing point stops on VN30F1M), natr normalizes by price level so volatility can be ranked cross-sectionally across assets trading at different nominal prices.
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Formulated as an exact ewm_mean(alpha=1.0 / period, adjust=False, min_samples=period) kernel in Rust.

docs.title: chandelier_exit(high, low, close, period=22, multiplier=3.0)
docs.text:
Chuck LeBeau's ATR Trailing Stop (pl.Struct: ("long_stop", "short_stop")):

\[ \text{LongStop}_t = \max_{0 \le i < n} H_{t-i} - m \cdot \text{ATR}_t(n), \qquad \text{ShortStop}_t = \min_{0 \le i < n} L_{t-i} + m \cdot \text{ATR}_t(n) \]

docs.title: ulcer_index(close, period=14)
docs.text:
Peter Martin's Downside Drawdown Volatility (1987): Unlike standard deviation (stddev), which penalizes upside rallies and downside crashes equally, ulcer_index measures the root-mean-square depth and duration of rolling percentage drawdowns:

\[ R_t = \frac{C_t - \max_{0 \le i < n} C_{t-i}}{\max_{0 \le i < n} C_{t-i}} \times 100 \le 0, \qquad \text{UI}_t(n) = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} R_{t-i}^2} \]

docs.title: chaikin_volatility(high, low, ema_period=10, roc_period=10)
docs.text:
Measures the rate of expansion or contraction of the smoothed High-Low trading range:

\[ \text{EMA}_{\text{HL}, t} = \text{EMA}_{n_1}(H_t - L_t), \qquad \text{ChaikinVol}_t = \frac{\text{EMA}_{\text{HL}, t} - \text{EMA}_{\text{HL}, t - n_2}}{\text{EMA}_{\text{HL}, t - n_2}} \times 100 \]

docs.title: 3. Dynamic Volatility & Breakout Channels
docs.text: Function Signature Midline (\(M_t\)) & Band Formulas (\(U_t, L_t\)) Output Type / Struct Fields bollinger_bands(close, period=20, std_dev=2.0) \(M_t = \text{SMA}_n(C_t)\), \(U_t / L_t = M_t \pm k\hat{\sigma}_t\)\(\text{Bandwidth}_t = \frac{U_t - L_t}{M_t} \times 100\), \(\%B_t = \frac{C_t - L_t}{U_t - L_t}\) Struct(upper, middle, lower, bandwidth, percent_b) bollinger_delta(close, period=20, std_dev=2.0) \(\Delta_{\text{BB}, t} = U_t - L_t = 2 k \hat{\sigma}_t\) Float64 keltner_channels(high, low, close, period=20, atr_period=10, multiplier=2.0) \(M_t = \text{EMA}_{n}(\text{TP}_t)\), \(U_t / L_t = M_t \pm m \cdot \text{ATR}_{n_{\text{atr}}}(t)\) Struct(upper, middle, lower) keltner_width(high, low, close, period=20, atr_period=10, multiplier=2.0) \(\text{KCWidth}_t = \frac{U_t - L_t}{M_t} = \frac{2 m \cdot \text{ATR}_t}{M_t}\) Float64 donchian_channels(high, low, period=20) \(U_t = \max_{0 \le i < n} H_{t-i}\), \(L_t = \min_{0 \le i < n} L_{t-i}\), \(M_t = \frac{U_t + L_t}{2}\) Struct(upper, middle, lower) donchian_width(high, low, period=20) \(\text{DCWidth}_t = \frac{U_t - L_t}{M_t} \times 100\) Float64 starc_bands(high, low, close, sma_period=6, atr_period=15, multiplier=2.0) \(M_t = \text{SMA}_{n_1}(C_t)\), \(U_t / L_t = M_t \pm m \cdot \text{ATR}_{n_2}(t)\) Struct(upper, middle, lower) envelopes(close, period=20, pct=0.025) \(M_t = \text{SMA}_n(C_t)\), \(U_t / L_t = M_t (1 \pm \text{pct})\) Struct(upper, middle, lower)

docs.title: Volume, Session VWAP & Money Flow (polars_anta.volume)
docs.text: The polars_anta.volume module provides 16 volume-weighted price benchmarks, execution bands, and money-flow oscillators designed to track accumulation/distribution and intraday fair value.

docs.title: vwap(high, low, close, volume, period=None)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation: Let Typical Price be \(\text{TP}_t = \frac{H_t + L_t + C_t}{3}\). - Cumulative Mode (period=None, default):

\[ \text{VWAP}_t = \frac{\sum_{\tau=1}^t \text{TP}_\tau \cdot V_\tau}{\sum_{\tau=1}^t V_\tau} \]
  • Rolling Window Mode (period=N):
\[ \text{VWAP}_t(N) = \frac{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \text{TP}_{t-k} \cdot V_{t-k}}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} V_{t-k}} \]

docs.title: vwap_bands(high, low, close, volume, period=None, mult1=1.0, mult2=2.0, mult3=3.0)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation (Volume-Weighted Standard Deviation Bands): Using the identity \(\text{Var}_V(\text{TP}) = \mathbb{E}_V[\text{TP}^2] - \left(\mathbb{E}_V[\text{TP}]\right)^2\):

\[ \sigma_{\text{VWAP}, t} = \sqrt{\max\left(0,\, \frac{\sum \text{TP}_\tau^2 \cdot V_\tau}{\sum V_\tau} - \text{VWAP}_t^2\right)} \] \[ \text{Upper}_{k, t} = \text{VWAP}_t + m_k \cdot \sigma_{\text{VWAP}, t}, \qquad \text{Lower}_{k, t} = \text{VWAP}_t - m_k \cdot \sigma_{\text{VWAP}, t} \quad (k \in \{1, 2, 3\}) \]

Returns a pl.Struct with fields ("vwap", "upper_1", "lower_1", "upper_2", "lower_2", "upper_3", "lower_3").

docs.title: session_vwap(high, low, close, volume, session_by=None, time_col="timestamp", mult1=1.0, mult2=2.0)
docs.text:
Session-Anchored VWAP with Deviation Z-Score: In intraday equity and index futures trading (such as VN30F1M), execution algorithms benchmark fills against the Session VWAP that resets at the start of every trading day (pl.col(time_col).dt.date() when session_by=None, or custom session identifiers such as morning/afternoon sessions).

\[ \text{VWAP}_{t \in S} = \frac{\sum_{\tau \in S, \tau \le t} \text{TP}_\tau V_\tau}{\sum_{\tau \in S, \tau \le t} V_\tau}, \qquad Z_{\text{VWAP}, t} = \frac{\text{TP}_t - \text{VWAP}_{t \in S}}{\sigma_{\text{VWAP}, t \in S}} \]
  • Output pl.Struct Schema (prefix="session_" when unnest=True): ("vwap", "upper_1", "lower_1", "upper_2", "lower_2", "zscore").
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Uses native Polars .cum_sum().over(session_key) window partitioning, resetting cumulative sums across thousands of trading sessions in parallel with zero loops.

docs.title: vwma(close, volume, period=20)
docs.text:
Volume-Weighted Moving Average:

\[ \text{VWMA}_t(n) = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} C_{t-i} \cdot V_{t-i}}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} V_{t-i}} \]

Comparing \(\text{VWMA}_t(n) - \text{SMA}_t(n)\) reveals whether volume is concentrated on high-price bars (bullish volume participation) or low-price bars.

docs.title: obv(close, volume) & pvt(close, volume)
docs.text:
• Joe Granville's On-Balance Volume (obv):
\[ \text{OBV}_t = \sum_{\tau=1}^t \text{sign}(C_\tau - C_{\tau-1}) \cdot V_\tau \]
  • Price Volume Trend (pvt): Scales signed volume by proportional price return rather than a binary step function:
\[ \text{PVT}_t = \sum_{\tau=1}^t \left(\frac{C_\tau - C_{\tau-1}}{C_{\tau-1}}\right) V_\tau \]

docs.title: adl(high, low, close, volume) & cmf(high, low, close, volume, period=20)
docs.text:
Both indicators rely on Marc Chaikin's Close Location Value (CLV), which locates the closing price within the bar's High-Low range \([-1, +1]\):

\[ \text{CLV}_t = \frac{(C_t - L_t) - (H_t - C_t)}{H_t - L_t} = \frac{2C_t - L_t - H_t}{H_t - L_t} \in [-1, +1] \]
  • Accumulation / Distribution Line (adl): \(\text{ADL}_t = \sum_{\tau=1}^t \text{CLV}_\tau \cdot V_\tau\).
  • Chaikin Money Flow (cmf): \(n\)-period ratio of Money Flow Volume to total volume:
\[ \text{CMF}_t(n) = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \text{CLV}_{t-i} \cdot V_{t-i}}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} V_{t-i}} \in [-1, +1] \]

docs.title: mfi(high, low, close, volume, period=14)
docs.text:
Quong & Soudack's Money Flow Index (Volume-Weighted RSI): Let Raw Money Flow be \(\text{RMF}_t = \text{TP}_t \cdot V_t\). Partitioning \(\text{RMF}_t\) into positive flow (\(\text{TP}_t > \text{TP}_{t-1}\)) and negative flow (\(\text{TP}_t < \text{TP}_{t-1}\)) over window \(n\):

\[ \text{MFR}_t = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \text{RMF}_{t-i}^+}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \text{RMF}_{t-i}^-}, \qquad \text{MFI}_t = 100 - \frac{100}{1 + \text{MFR}_t} \in [0, 100] \]

docs.title: klinger(high, low, close, volume, fast_period=34, slow_period=55, signal_period=13)
docs.text:
Stephen Klinger's Volume Force Oscillator: Combines trend direction \(T_t = \text{sign}(\text{TP}_t - \text{TP}_{t-1})\), daily range \(dm_t = H_t - L_t\), and cumulative trend range \(cm_t\) into Volume Force \(\text{VF}_t = V_t \cdot \left|2\frac{dm_t}{cm_t} - 1\right| \cdot T_t \cdot 100\), then computes:

\[ \text{KVO}_t = \text{EMA}_{34}(\text{VF}_t) - \text{EMA}_{55}(\text{VF}_t), \qquad \text{Signal}_t = \text{EMA}_{13}(\text{KVO}_t) \]

Returns pl.Struct with fields ("klinger", "signal").

docs.title: eom, force_index, nvi, pvi, vpci, vr
docs.text: Function Signature Mathematical Definition Quantitative Interpretation eom(high, low, volume, period=14, scale=10000.0) \(\text{SMA}_n\left(\Delta\left(\frac{H_t + L_t}{2}\right) \cdot \frac{H_t - L_t}{V_t / \text{scale}}\right)\) Richard Arms' Ease of Movement: high positive values mean price advances on light volume (low overhead resistance). force_index(close, volume, period=13) \(\text{EMA}_n\left((C_t - C_{t-1}) \cdot V_t\right)\) Alexander Elder's Force Index combining direction, extent of price change, and volume. nvi(close, volume) / pvi(close, volume) Updates cumulative return index only on bars where \(V_t < V_{t-1}\) (nvi) or \(V_t > V_{t-1}\) (pvi) Norman Fosback's Smart-Money (nvi, active on quiet volume days) vs. Crowd-Activity (pvi) indices. vpci(close, volume, short_period=5, long_period=20) \(\text{VPC}_t \times \text{VPR}_t \times \text{VM}_t\) Buff Dormeier's Volume Price Confirmation Indicator measuring divergence between VWMA and SMA. vr(close, volume, period=26) \(\frac{\text{AV}_n + \frac{1}{2}\text{CV}_n}{\text{BV}_n + \frac{1}{2}\text{CV}_n} \times 100\) Up-Volume (\(\text{AV}_n\)) vs. Down-Volume (\(\text{BV}_n\)) Ratio.

docs.title: How Many Technical and Formulaic Alphas Survive Multiple-Testing and Transaction-Cost Falsification on Vietnamese Equities?
docs.text: Pre-Specified Empirical Study (polars-anta Factor Zoo) Analysis-Plan Commit: 4c1a4b559d22a1367ce46b513ab7ff1079fff360 (PREREGISTRATION.md) Signal Registry SHA-256: 8aa3c11b97810083b875084d38cfda6df1994de38ec9b077faeaf46dc31c948c (\(K = 150\) signals, \(146\) unique)

docs.title: 1. TL;DR
docs.text:
• 150 signals collapse to ~6 effective independent dimensions (\(N_{\text{eff}} = 6.00\)): Out of 150 pre-specified daily OHLCV signals (146 unique after accounting for 4 exact duplicate pairs) evaluated at default parameters on the point-in-time top-150 liquid Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE) universe during Discovery (2014-01-01 to 2021-12-31, \(1{,}998\) trading days, \(h = 5\) open-to-open days), 91 pass raw Stationary Bootstrap \(p \le 0.05\) (95 have Newey–West \(|t| \ge 1.96\), vs. \(7.5\) expected by chance under independence). Eigenvalue decomposition of the \(150 \times 150\) daily IC correlation matrix reveals an effective independent test count of \(N_{\text{eff}} = 6.00\) (\(\lambda_1 = 55.21\), top 5 principal components explain \(66.6\%\) of variance; \(N_{\text{eff}} = 6.13\) across the 146 unique signals).
  • The dominant short-horizon reversal factor is statistically genuine and replicates out of sample: After joint multiple-testing correction and OLS-CUSUM structural stability screening, 94 signals pass Benjamini–Hochberg FDR (\(q \le 0.10\)), 71 pass Romano–Wolf stepdown FWER (\(\alpha \le 0.05\)), and 64 are classified as structurally stable (robust) while 14 are flagged as decaying. In the locked Holdout sample (2022-01-01 to 2026-11-10, \(1{,}202\) valid \(5\)-day return sessions), cross-sectional Rank IC correlates at \(r = 0.77\) (\(0.7675\)) with Discovery across all 150 signals, and 38 of the 64 (59.4%) robust discovery signals replicate under Romano–Wolf FWER (\(p_{\text{RW}} \le 0.05\)) with a median IC retention ratio of \(97.6\%\) (\(0.9764\)).
  • Zero standalone single-factor strategies survive long-only execution after retail HOSE costs: When the 80 non-decaying discovery survivors (64 robust + 16 fdr_only) are implemented as 5-day rebalanced, equal-weighted long-only top-quintile (Q5) portfolios against the equal-weight universe under retail HOSE execution frictions (0.15%/side brokerage + 0.10%/side slippage + 0.10% statutory sell tax = 30 bps per unit of L1 weight turnover \(\sum_i |w_{i,t} - w_{i,t-1}|\), or 60 bps round-trip replacement cost), the top-6 \(|t_{\text{NW}}|\) fast mean-reversion signals face 5-day L1 turnover of 1.28–1.74 (63.8%–87.2% one-way) and breakeven cost ceilings of only -6.7–20.5 bps round-trip (5.7–20.5 bps among the 5 with positive gross Q5 excess). Only 2 slower momentum signals (trix_15 at \(+8.37\%/\text{yr}\), raw \(p = 0.0170\); tsi at \(+7.65\%/\text{yr}\), raw \(p = 0.0320\)) clear the cost hurdle at unadjusted \(p \le 0.05\), 0 survive Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment (\(q \le 0.10\)) across the 80 cost-stage candidates, and 0 survive in the locked Holdout.
  • Exploratory post-holdout diagnostics explain the gap between statistical IC and long-only net returns (§8.3): (a) Cross-sectionally orthogonalizing all 150 signals against 5-day close-to-close return reversal (rev_5_rank) raises \(N_{\text{eff}}\) from \(6.00\) to \(9.37\) and leaves 91 robust discovery signals, 40 of which replicate in Holdout under Romano–Wolf \(p_{\text{RW}} \le 0.05\); (b) Q1–Q5 active return decomposition shows that \(65.5\%\) of the top-10 signals' \(\text{Q5} - \text{Q1}\) spread in Discovery (\(90.0\%\) in Holdout) originates in the short leg (Q1 underperformance), which cannot be shorted on HOSE; and (c) evaluating round-trip costs across 0–60 bps shows that 0 standalone 5-day Q5 strategies survive BH \(q \le 0.10\) at any cost \(\ge 30\text{ bps}\) round-trip in Discovery or \(\ge 10\text{ bps}\) in Holdout.

docs.title: 2. Motivation
docs.text:
Modern empirical asset pricing faces a well-documented Factor Zoo problem: when researchers test hundreds of correlated technical indicators and formulaic alphas on the same historical panel, conventional single-hypothesis \(t\)-thresholds (\(|t| \ge 1.96\)) produce massive false-discovery rates (Harvey, Liu & Zhu 2016; Chordia, Goyal & Saretto 2020). While recent work shows that many equity anomalies share a common statistical component that replicates better than naive uniform priors suggest once shrunken via Empirical Bayes (Jensen, Kelly & Pedersen 2023), a critical gap remains between frictionless cross-sectional predictability (Rank IC) and net-of-cost implementability in emerging markets (Hou, Xue & Zhang 2020; Novy-Marx & Velikov 2016).

Rather than marketing polars-anta as a collection of "200+ fast alpha indicators", this study subjects the library's entire daily-OHLCV indicator and WorldQuant formulaic alpha catalog (\(K = 150\) scale-free signals) to a pre-specified statistical and economic falsification funnel on Vietnamese equities (HOSE), using the inference machinery built into polars_anta.inference.

docs.title: 3. Pre-Specified Analysis Plan & Anti-Data-Mining Protocol
docs.text:
To constrain hindsight bias, parameter tuning, and post-hoc threshold selection, the experimental design was specified and committed prior to running the discovery and holdout pipelines:

  • Analysis Plan Document: research/factor_zoo/PREREGISTRATION.md
  • Frozen Configuration: research/factor_zoo/config.py
  • Frozen Signal Registry: research/factor_zoo/registry.py
  • Git Analysis-Plan Commit Hash: 4c1a4b559d22a1367ce46b513ab7ff1079fff360
  • Registry Canonical SHA-256: 8aa3c11b97810083b875084d38cfda6df1994de38ec9b077faeaf46dc31c948c
  • Programmatic Holdout Guard: verify_preregistration_guard() in research/factor_zoo/pipeline.py refuses to execute --stage holdout unless --unlock-holdout is explicitly passed, PREREGISTRATION.md is committed to Git, and git status --porcelain confirms zero uncommitted modifications to PREREGISTRATION.md, config.py, and registry.py.

docs.title: 4.1 Source & Sample Period
docs.text: Daily OHLCV bars were retrieved from public Vietnamese equity market endpoints—primary VNDirect (api-finfo.vndirect.com.vn ticker directory and dchart-api.vndirect.com.vn daily history) with SSI iBoard (iboard-query.ssi.com.vn) as automatic fallback—for all 392 three-letter common equity tickers listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE), spanning 2012-03-19 through 2026-11-10 (1,138,548 raw ticker-day observations). The period 2012-03-19 to 2013-12-31 serves strictly as a warm-up buffer for rolling lookback windows and the 250-day listing-age filter.

docs.title: 4.3 Point-in-Time Liquid Investable Universe (in_universe)
docs.text:
On each trading date \(t \in [\text{2014-01-02}, \text{2026-11-10}]\) (3,206 trading days), a stock enters the investable cross-section if and only if using information available at \(\text{close}_t\): 1. Cumulative trading history is at least 250 valid sessions, 2. Closing price \(C_{i,t} \ge \mathbf{5{,}000\text{ VND}}\), and 3. 60-session rolling median daily traded value (\(\text{close} \times \text{volume}\)) ranks in the top 150 eligible stocks on date \(t\).

This yields 463,707 ticker-day observations across 364 unique tickers (median 150.0 stocks/day, max 150, min 17 on the first days of 2014): - Discovery Sample (2014-01-02 to 2021-12-31): 1,998 trading days, 282,507 universe rows, 340 unique tickers. - Locked Holdout Sample (2022-01-01 to 2026-11-10): 1,208 trading days (1,202 sessions with complete 5-day forward open-to-open returns), 181,200 universe rows, 250 unique tickers.

docs.title: 5. Signal Registry & Scale-Free Normalization
docs.text:
All 150 daily-OHLCV-compatible signals in polars-anta are evaluated at their exact library default parameters (0 hyperparameter sweeps):

  • Scale-Free Transformation: Price-level overlays (moving averages, bands, stops, pivots, channels) are mapped to dimensionless ratios relative to close (e.g., close / sma(close, 10) - 1, Bollinger percent_b, (close - supertrend) / close, (close - pivot_p) / close). Multi-field pl.Struct indicators select one canonical primary component (see registry.py).
  • Cross-Sectional Ranking: Each signal is computed per ticker (.over("ticker")) and then mapped to a uniform cross-sectional percentile rank within the active universe on each day \(t\) via cs_rank(..., over="date").
  • Two-Sided Testing: Every signal is tested once (alternative="two-sided"), preventing researcher degrees of freedom in flipping factor signs.

docs.title: 6. Statistical & Economic Methodology
docs.text:
Full mathematical formulations and Monte Carlo size/power validations of the inference estimators are documented in docs/indicators/inference.md and docs/assets/inference_size_power.md.

  1. Target Return: Next-day open-to-open return over \(h = 5\) trading sessions, \(r_{i,t,5} = \text{open}_{i,t+6}/\text{open}_{i,t+1} - 1\). Signals observed at \(\text{close}_t\) are assumed executed at \(\text{open}_{t+1}\) (zero look-ahead bias).
  2. Cross-Sectional Information Coefficient (ic_matrix): Daily cross-sectional Spearman rank correlation \(\text{IC}_{k,t}\) between factor \(k\)'s universe rank at \(\text{close}_t\) and \(r_{i,t,5}\).
  3. Autocorrelation-Robust Inference (falsify_factors): Because overlapping 5-day forward returns induce \(\text{MA}(4)\) serial correlation in daily \(\text{IC}_{k,t}\), standard errors use the Bartlett-kernel Newey–West HAC estimator with \(L = 4\) lags, and resampling uses the Politis–Romano (1994) Stationary Bootstrap with geometric block lengths (\(\text{mean\_block} = \max(5, T^{1/3}) = 12.60\), \(B = 2{,}000\), seed = 20261110).
  4. Multiple-Testing Control (adjust_pvalues, romano_wolf):
  5. Benjamini–Hochberg (1995) FDR at \(q = 0.10\) across all \(K = 150\) signals.
  6. Romano–Wolf (2005, 2016) Stepdown FWER at \(\alpha = 0.05\), resampling all \(K = 150\) IC series using identical stationary block bootstrap indices to preserve the cross-factor dependence structure.
  7. Empirical-Bayes Effect-Size Shrinkage (eb_shrink): Sample mean ICs \(\overline{\text{IC}}_k\) are shrunken toward zero (prior="zero") using the Efron–Morris (1973) / Jensen–Kelly–Pedersen (2023) empirical-Bayes precision weights \(\widehat{\text{IC}}^{\text{EB}}_k = \frac{\hat{\tau}^2}{\hat{\tau}^2 + s_k^2}\overline{\text{IC}}_k\).
  8. Structural Break Screening (cusum_mean_test): Brown–Durbin–Evans (1975) / Ploberger–Krämer (1992) OLS-CUSUM test with Newey–West long-run variance (\(L = 4\)). Statistically significant signals with p_cusum <= 0.05 whose second-half \(|{\text{IC}}|\) is smaller than first-half \(|{\text{IC}}|\) are classified as decaying.
  9. Long-Only Transaction-Cost Stage (bootstrap_test, breakeven_cost): Because short selling underlying equities is not practically available on HOSE, all non-decaying statistical survivors (verdict in {"robust", "fdr_only"}, \(80\) signals) are evaluated as long-only top-quintile (Q5) equal-weighted portfolios (oriented by discovery \(\text{sign}(\overline{\text{IC}}_k)\)), rebalanced every \(5\) trading days against the equal-weighted investable universe. Transaction costs deduct 0.15%/side brokerage + 0.10%/side slippage + 0.10% statutory sell tax (30 bps per unit of L1 weight turnover \(\sum_i |w_{i,t} - w_{i,t-1}|\), equivalent to 60 bps per full one-way portfolio replacement). Survival requires one-sided Stationary Bootstrap \(p \le 0.05\) on net active returns, BH \(q \le 0.10\) across cost-stage candidates, and breakeven_cost \(> 30\text{ bps}\) L1 (60 bps round-trip).

docs.title: 7.2 Why 91 of 150 Signals Pass Raw \(p \le 0.05\): Effective Independent Tests (\(N_{\text{eff}} = 6.00\))
docs.text:
A researcher testing 150 indicators might assume they have conducted 150 independent experiments. Spectral decomposition of the \(150 \times 150\) daily Spearman IC correlation matrix in Discovery (2014–2021) refutes this: - Largest Eigenvalue (\(\lambda_1\)): \(55.21\) (\(36.8\%\) of total variance across all 150 signals). - Top 5 Principal Components: Explain \(66.6\%\) (\(0.6660\)) of total cross-signal IC variance. - Participation Ratio (\(N_{\text{eff}} = (\sum \lambda_k)^2 / \sum \lambda_k^2\)): \(6.00\) (\(6.0041\)) effective independent dimensions.

Because the vast majority of technical oscillators, moving-average ratios, price-channel positions, and short-window WorldQuant alphas load heavily on the same underlying 5-day cross-sectional mean-reversion / overreaction factor on HOSE, when that single latent factor carries a strong \(t\)-statistic (\(|t| > 10\)), dozens of algebraically related indicators simultaneously clear \(|t| \ge 1.96\) and Romano–Wolf FWER thresholds.

docs.title: 7.4 Transaction-Cost Falsification Stage: Why High-IC Signals Fail Long-Only Execution
docs.text:
When the 80 non-decaying discovery survivors (64 robust + 16 fdr_only) are formed into 5-day rebalanced long-only top-quintile (Q5) portfolios against the equal-weight universe (descriptive ranges derived automatically in results/discovery/cost_stage_summary.json): 1. 68 of 80 candidates yield negative net active returns after HOSE fees, slippage, and sell tax (60 bps round-trip replacement cost; across all 68 negative-net signals, 5-day L1 turnover spans \(0.27\text{–}1.83\), or \(13.5\%\text{–}91.4\%\) one-way replacement, with annualized cost drag of \(4.1\%\text{–}27.6\%/\text{yr}\) and breakeven round-trip costs of \(-23.8\text{–}53.1\text{ bps}\)). The top-6 \(|t_{\text{NW}}|\) fast reversal signals (returns_divergence_14, hma_10, tema_10, zlema_10, true_range_norm, alpha_018) exhibit 5-day L1 weight turnover of \(1.28\text{–}1.74\) (\(63.8\%\text{–}87.2\%\) one-way portfolio replacement every 5 trading days), incurring an annualized cost drag of \(19.3\%\text{–}26.4\%/\text{yr}\), while their long-only top-quintile gross excess returns correspond to breakeven round-trip costs of only \(-6.7\text{–}20.5\text{ bps}\) (\(5.7\text{–}20.5\text{ bps}\) across the 5 signals with positive gross Q5 excess). docs.title: 9. Limitations
docs.text:
1. Survivorship Bias in Public Exchange Directory: The public exchange directory query (VNDirect / SSI iBoard) returned 392 currently listed 3-letter HOSE equities (0 historical delisted tickers; only 2 cached tickers have a last trading date before 2026-10-01: LGC ending 2026-04-29 with 2,801 bars and TTE ending 2026-07-01 with 1,021 bars, see results/audit/data_adjustment_check.json). Although the point-in-time rolling 60-day median traded value filter (top 150, minimum 5,000 VND, minimum 250 trading sessions) excludes distressed micro-caps as liquidity deteriorates, historical delistings between 2012 and 2026 are absent from the public feed.
  2. Corporate-Action & Price-Adjustment Uncertainty in Public Feeds: Across 1,138,156 raw 1-day return observations in the cached feed, 5,737 exceed \(\pm 7.5\%\) (5,653 after zero-volume filtering), 343 exceed \(\pm 15\%\) (126 negative, 217 positive), and 32 exceed \(\pm 30\%\). Out of the 343 moves exceeding \(\pm 15\%\), 78 (22.74%) fall within \(\pm 0.015\) of typical stock-dividend or split price ratios (44 near 5:6, 25 near 4:5, 7 near 10:13, 2 near 2:3). Whether the upstream public history endpoint is partially adjusted or unadjusted for corporate actions is not independently verified; the cleaning pipeline mitigates single-day discontinuities by dropping observations with \(|C_t / C_{t-1} - 1| > 7.5\%\).
  3. Daily Typical-Price VWAP Proxy: For formulaic alphas requiring vwap (alpha_001–alpha_101), intraday trade-by-trade VWAP is unavailable in public daily feeds and is proxied by daily typical price \((H_t + L_t + C_t)/3\).
  4. Long-Only Constraint & Equal-Weight Rebalancing: Evaluating each signal as a standalone 5-day rebalanced equal-weighted Q5 portfolio without turnover regularization (e.g., no buffer banding, no multi-factor combination, no trade-off against expected transaction cost) represents a deliberately harsh falsification benchmark. Combining the \(N_{\text{eff}} = 6.00\) orthogonal dimensions with a turnover-penalized optimizer is the natural next step beyond single-factor falsification.
  5. Retail Transaction Cost Schedule: The pre-specified 60 bps round-trip cost (0.15%/side brokerage + 0.10%/side slippage + 0.10% statutory sell tax, confirmed post-hoc on 2026-11-11) reflects standard Vietnamese retail commission tiers and is constant across stocks and time, whereas institutional brokerage fees can be lower while price impact scales non-linearly with order size relative to daily volume.
  6. Exact and Near-Duplicate Signals in the Frozen Registry: As documented in results/audit/duplicate_signals.json, the 150 registered entries contain 4 exact duplicate pairs (146 unique signals) and 12 near-duplicate pairs with \(|\text{corr}| > 0.99\). While the participation ratio (\(N_{\text{eff}} = 6.00\)) and Romano–Wolf joint bootstrap naturally account for collinearity, a 146-unique-signal sensitivity check is reported in §8.3.
  7. Cross-Sectional Breadth (\(N \le 150\)): Compared to US CRSP panels (\(N \approx 3{,}000\)), a 150-stock universe has higher idiosyncratic portfolio variance in each quintile (30 stocks per quintile).
